  # --- Launch Template for Spark Nodes (attaches shared-infra EMR security group) ---

  SparkLaunchTemplate:
    Type: AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate
    Properties:
      LaunchTemplateName: !Sub "${ProjectName}-emr-spark-nodes-lt"
      LaunchTemplateData:
        MetadataOptions:
          HttpTokens: required
          HttpPutResponseHopLimit: 2
        SecurityGroupIds:
          - !Ref EmrClusterSg
          - !Ref EmrCelebornAccessSg
        TagSpecifications:
          - ResourceType: instance
            Tags:
              - Key: Name
                Value: !Sub "${ProjectName}-emr-spark-node"
              - Key: Project
                Value: !Ref ProjectName

  # --- General Node Group (system pods: CoreDNS, kube-proxy, etc.) ---

  GeneralNodeGroup:
    Type: AWS::EKS::Nodegroup
    DependsOn: EksCluster
    Properties:
      NodegroupName: !Sub "${ProjectName}-emr-general"
      ClusterName: !Ref EksCluster
      NodeRole: !GetAtt NodeGroupRole.Arn
      Subnets:
        - !Ref EksPrivateSubnet1
        - !Ref EksPrivateSubnet2
      InstanceTypes:
        - !Ref GeneralInstanceType
      ScalingConfig:
        MinSize: !Ref GeneralMinSize
        DesiredSize: !Ref GeneralDesiredSize
        MaxSize: !Ref GeneralMaxSize
      AmiType: AL2023_x86_64_STANDARD
      CapacityType: ON_DEMAND
      DiskSize: 50
      Labels:
        node-type: general
        node-lifecycle: on-demand
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub "${ProjectName}-emr-general-nodes"
        Project: !Ref ProjectName

  # --- Spark Node Group (EMR executor pods) ---

  SparkNodeGroup:
    Type: AWS::EKS::Nodegroup
    DependsOn: EksCluster
    Properties:
      NodegroupName: !Sub "${ProjectName}-emr-spark"
      ClusterName: !Ref EksCluster
      NodeRole: !GetAtt NodeGroupRole.Arn
      Subnets:
        - !Ref EksPrivateSubnet1
        - !Ref EksPrivateSubnet2
      LaunchTemplate:
        Id: !Ref SparkLaunchTemplate
        Version: !GetAtt SparkLaunchTemplate.LatestVersionNumber
      InstanceTypes:
        - !Ref SparkInstanceType
      ScalingConfig:
        MinSize: !Ref SparkMinSize
        DesiredSize: !Ref SparkDesiredSize
        MaxSize: !Ref SparkMaxSize
      AmiType: AL2023_x86_64_STANDARD
      CapacityType: ON_DEMAND
      Labels:
        node-type: spark
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub "${ProjectName}-emr-spark-nodes"
        Project: !Ref ProjectName

  # --- EBS CSI Driver Addon ---
  # NOTE: The aws-ebs-csi-driver addon is NOT deployed here because it requires
  # an IRSA trust policy on EBSCSIDriverRole. The OIDC provider is only available
  # after the EKS cluster stack deploys, so the trust policy cannot be set in
  # CloudFormation at stack-creation time. Without the correct trust policy, the
  # addon pods cannot assume the role, they crash-loop, and CloudFormation hangs
  # indefinitely in CREATE_IN_PROGRESS.
  # The addon is instead installed via CLI in deploy.sh after OIDC/IRSA setup.

Outputs:
  GeneralNodeGroupName:
    Description: Name of the general node group
    Value: !Ref GeneralNodeGroup
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${ProjectName}-EmrGeneralNodeGroup"

  SparkNodeGroupName:
    Description: Name of the Spark node group
    Value: !Ref SparkNodeGroup
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${ProjectName}-EmrSparkNodeGroup"

  EBSCSIDriverRoleName:
    Description: IAM role name for EBS CSI driver (trust policy updated by deploy script)
    Value: !Ref EBSCSIDriverRole
    Export:
      Name: !Sub "${ProjectName}-EmrEBSCSIRoleName"

Description: Block application network traffic from experiment Region to target Region and pause cross-Region replication

    Type: String

  Duration:
    Type: String

  Region:
    Type: String
    Default: us-west-2
    Description: The region in which the actions will be performed

  TransitGatewayTagValue:
    Type: String

    Description: The value of the tag for identifying the Transit Gateway

  SubnetTagValue:
    Type: String
    Default: true
    Description: The value of the tag for identifying the Subnet

  S3BucketTagValue:
    Type: String
    Default: true

    Type: String

Resources:
  MultiRegionScenario:
    Type: AWS::FIS::ExperimentTemplate
    Properties:
      Description: Block application network traffic from experiment Region to target Region and pause cross-Region replication
      RoleArn: !GetAtt ExperimentRole.Arn
      Targets:
        TransitGateway:
          ResourceType: aws:ec2:transit-gateway
          ResourceTags:
            ChaosAllowed: !Ref TransitGatewayTagValue
          SelectionMode: ALL
        Subnet:
          ResourceType: aws:ec2:subnet
          ResourceTags:
            ChaosAllowed: !Ref SubnetTagValue
          SelectionMode: ALL
        S3Bucket:
          ResourceType: aws:s3:bucket
          ResourceTags:
            ChaosAllowed: !Ref S3BucketTagValue
          SelectionMode: ALL
        DynamoDBGlobalTable:
          ResourceType: aws:dynamodb:global-table
          ResourceTags:
            ChaosAllowed: !Ref DynamoDBTagValue
          SelectionMode: ALL
      Actions:
        DisruptTransitGatewayConnectivity:
          ActionId: aws:network:transit-gateway-disrupt-cross-region-connectivity
          Parameters:
            duration: !Ref Duration
            region: !Ref Region
          Targets:
            TransitGateways: TransitGateway
        DisruptSubnetConnectivity:
          ActionId: aws:network:route-table-disrupt-cross-region-connectivity
          Parameters:
            duration: !Ref Duration
            region: !Ref Region
          Targets:
            Subnets: Subnet
        PauseS3Replication:
          ActionId: aws:s3:bucket-pause-replication
          Parameters:
            duration: !Ref Duration
            region: !Ref Region
          Targets:
            Buckets: S3Bucket
        PauseDynamoDBReplication:
          ActionId: aws:dynamodb:global-table-pause-replication
          Parameters:
            duration: !Ref Duration
          Targets:
            Tables: DynamoDBGlobalTable
      StopConditions:
        - Source: none
      LogConfiguration:
        LogSchemaVersion: 2
        CloudWatchLogsConfiguration:
          LogGroupArn: !GetAtt FISExperimentLogGroup.Arn
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub 'Cross-Region: Connectivity to ${Region}'
        Env: !Ref Env

    Type: AWS::IAM::Role

            reason: "Wildcard permissions are required for FIS experiments to cover VPCs."
            appliesTo: ["Resource::arn:aws:ec2:*:*:vpc/*"]
          - id: AwsSolutions-IAM5
            reason: "Wildcard permissions are required for FIS experiments to cover network interfaces."

          - id: AwsSolutions-IAM5

          - id: AwsSolutions-IAM5

            appliesTo: ["Resource::arn:aws:ec2:*:*:security-group/*"]
          - id: AwsSolutions-IAM5

              - Effect: Allow

                  - 'ec2:DescribeVpcs'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeManagedPrefixLists'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSubnets'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeNetworkAcls'
                Resource: '*'
                Condition:

              - Effect: Allow

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained ECS Fargate microservice that registers itself with a private Cloud Map service discovery namespace so other services in the same environment can find it by DNS name. The stack should build its own VPC with a public subnet, two private subnets across separate availability zones, an internet gateway, and a NAT gateway for the private subnets, along with an ECS cluster and a security group allowing the containers to communicate with each other within the VPC's CIDR range. It should accept parameters for the environment name, service name, container image, container port (defaulting to port 80 on the nginx image), CPU and memory, and desired task count (defaulting to two tasks), plus an optional custom IAM role the containers can assume for accessing other AWS resources. Provision the ECS task execution role, a CloudWatch log group for the container logs, and a Cloud Map service so the ECS service can be discovered via a private DNS SRV record. Finally, configure application auto scaling on the ECS service between two and ten tasks, scaling down when average CPU utilization drops to or below 20 percent and scaling up in graduated steps when it climbs to or above 70 percent, each change triggered by its own CloudWatch alarm.
ground_truth_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Deploy a service into an ECS cluster with service discovery endpoint
Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: The name of the environment to add this service to
  ServiceName:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: A name for the service
  ImageUrl:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: The url of a docker image that contains the application process that
      will handle the traffic for this service
  ContainerPort:
    Type: Number
    Default: 80
    Description: What port number the application inside the docker container is binding to
  ContainerCpu:
    Type: Number
    Default: 256
    Description: How much CPU to give the container. 1024 is 1 CPU
  ContainerMemory:
    Type: Number
    Default: 512
    Description: How much memory in megabytes to give the container
  DesiredCount:
    Type: Number
    Default: 2
    Description: How many copies of the service task to run
  Role:
    Type: String
    Default: ""
    Description: (Optional) An IAM role to give the service's containers if the code within needs to
      access other AWS resources like S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, etc

Conditions:
  HasCustomRole: !Not [ !Equals [!Ref 'Role', ''] ]

Resources:
  # This microservice used to be one of several stacks in a shared
  # reference architecture, importing ClusterName/PrivateServiceDiscovery
  # Namespace/AutoscalingRole via Fn::ImportValue from sibling stacks this
  # benchmark never included. Made self-contained: builds its own VPC (NAT
  # Gateway + private subnets so Fargate tasks can still pull the image and
  # ship logs), ECS Cluster, and Cloud Map namespace inline. Despite the
  # "-ec2-" in the filename, the original TaskDefinition set neither
  # NetworkMode nor RequiresCompatibilities, so it's converted to Fargate
  # here rather than also standing up a real EC2 Auto Scaling capacity
  # fleet just to keep an implicit launch-type default.
  Vpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
  VpcGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetOneRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.2.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetTwoRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.3.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  NatEip:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
  NatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatEip.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
  PrivateRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PrivateRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway
  PrivateSubnetOneRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
  PrivateSubnetTwoRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable

  Cluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Ref EnvironmentName

  ServiceDiscoveryNamespace:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::PrivateDnsNamespace
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}.local'
      Vpc: !Ref Vpc

  ContainerSecurityGroupRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-containers'
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: '-1'
          CidrIp: 10.0.0.0/16

  ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy

  AutoscalingRoleRes:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonEC2ContainerServiceAutoscaleRole

  # A log group for storing the stdout logs from this service's containers
  LogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}

  # The task definition. This is a simple metadata description of what
  # container to run, and what resource requirements it has.
  TaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
      Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes.Arn
      TaskRoleArn:
        Fn::If:
          - 'HasCustomRole'
          - !Ref 'Role'
          - !Ref "AWS::NoValue"
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
          Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
          Image: !Ref 'ImageUrl'
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: 'awslogs'
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}
              awslogs-region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
              awslogs-stream-prefix: !Ref 'ServiceName'

  # The service. The service is a resource which allows you to run multiple
  # copies of a type of task, and gather up their logs and metrics, as well
  # as monitor the number of running tasks and replace any that have crashed
  Service:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    DependsOn: ServiceDiscoveryService
    Properties:
      ServiceName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cluster: !Ref Cluster
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      DeploymentConfiguration:
        MaximumPercent: 200
        MinimumHealthyPercent: 75
      DesiredCount: !Ref 'DesiredCount'
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          AssignPublicIp: DISABLED
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref ContainerSecurityGroupRes
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      TaskDefinition: !Ref 'TaskDefinition'
      ServiceRegistries:
        - RegistryArn: !GetAtt ServiceDiscoveryService.Arn
          ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          ContainerName: !Ref 'ServiceName'

  # Create a service discovery service in the private service namespace.
  ServiceDiscoveryService:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::Service
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref ServiceName
      DnsConfig:
        DnsRecords: [{Type: SRV, TTL: "10"}]
        NamespaceId: !GetAtt ServiceDiscoveryNamespace.Id
      HealthCheckCustomConfig:
        FailureThreshold: 1

  # Enable autoscaling for this service
  ScalableTarget:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalableTarget
    DependsOn: Service
    Properties:
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ResourceId:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - service
            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      MinCapacity: 2
      MaxCapacity: 10
      RoleARN:
        !GetAtt AutoscalingRoleRes.Arn

  # Create scaling policies for the service
  ScaleDownPolicy:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy
    DependsOn: ScalableTarget
    Properties:
      PolicyName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - scale
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - down
      PolicyType: StepScaling
      ResourceId:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - service
            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      StepScalingPolicyConfiguration:
        AdjustmentType: 'ChangeInCapacity'
        StepAdjustments:
          - MetricIntervalUpperBound: 0
            ScalingAdjustment: -1
        MetricAggregationType: 'Average'
        Cooldown: 60

  ScaleUpPolicy:
    Type: AWS::ApplicationAutoScaling::ScalingPolicy
    DependsOn: ScalableTarget
    Properties:
      PolicyName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - scale
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - up
      PolicyType: StepScaling
      ResourceId:
        Fn::Join:
          - '/'
          - - service
            - !Ref Cluster
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      ScalableDimension: 'ecs:service:DesiredCount'
      ServiceNamespace: 'ecs'
      StepScalingPolicyConfiguration:
        AdjustmentType: 'ChangeInCapacity'
        StepAdjustments:
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 0
            MetricIntervalUpperBound: 15
            ScalingAdjustment: 1
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 15
            MetricIntervalUpperBound: 25
            ScalingAdjustment: 2
          - MetricIntervalLowerBound: 25
            ScalingAdjustment: 3
        MetricAggregationType: 'Average'
        Cooldown: 60

  # Create alarms to trigger these policies
  LowCpuUsageAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '-'
          - - low-cpu
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      AlarmDescription:
        Fn::Join:
          - ' '
          - - "Low CPU utilization for service"
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - "in environment"
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/ECS
      Dimensions:
        - Name: ServiceName
          Value: !Ref 'ServiceName'
        - Name: ClusterName
          Value:
            !Ref Cluster
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 20
      ComparisonOperator: LessThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref ScaleDownPolicy

  HighCpuUsageAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName:
        Fn::Join:
          - '-'
          - - high-cpu
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
      AlarmDescription:
        Fn::Join:
          - ' '
          - - "High CPU utilization for service"
            - !Ref 'ServiceName'
            - "in environment"
            - !Ref 'EnvironmentName'
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/ECS
      Dimensions:
        - Name: ServiceName
          Value: !Ref 'ServiceName'
        - Name: ClusterName
          Value:
            !Ref Cluster
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 70
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref ScaleUpPolicy

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained AWS network backbone designed for hybrid interconnect demonstrations with an OCI primary region, including a VPC, an internet gateway, a private subnet in the first available availability zone, a route table with a default route via the IGW, a transit gateway with a VPC attachment, and a security group that only allows HTTPS inbound from a configurable internal CIDR range and only allows HTTPS outbound to the OCI backbone CIDR; it should also conditionally create a customer gateway and VPN connection to OCI using static routes only, and define a transit gateway route for OCI traffic, all while enabling VPC flow logs encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key that has key rotation enabled and logs stored in CloudWatch with a 30-day retention, and ensuring that all resources use parameterized CIDRs with defaults of 10.94.0.0/16 for the VPC and 10.94.10.0/24 for the subnet.
ground_truth_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: AWS network backbone resources paired with OCI-primary DRG backbone.

Parameters:
  BackboneVpcCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.94.0.0/16
  BackboneSubnetCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.94.10.0/24
  AllowedIngressCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.0.0/8
  EnableSiteToSiteVpn:
    Type: String
    Default: "true"
    AllowedValues:
      - "true"
      - "false"
  OciCustomerGatewayPublicIp:
    Type: String
    Default: 198.51.100.10
  OciBackboneCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.54.0.0/16
  OciBgpAsn:
    Type: Number
    Default: 31898

Conditions:
  EnableSiteToSiteVpnCondition: !Equals [!Ref EnableSiteToSiteVpn, "true"]

Resources:
  BackboneVpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: !Ref BackboneVpcCidr
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-vpc-backbone'

  BackboneLogKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub '${AWS::StackName} VPC flow log encryption key'
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableAccountAdministration
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: kms:*
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowCloudWatchLogsUse
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: !Sub 'logs.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
            Action:
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:DescribeKey
              - kms:Encrypt
              - kms:GenerateDataKey
              - kms:ReEncrypt*
            Resource: '*'

  BackboneFlowLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      KmsKeyId: !GetAtt BackboneLogKey.Arn
      RetentionInDays: 30

  BackboneFlowLogRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: write-vpc-flow-logs
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                  - logs:DescribeLogStreams
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub '${BackboneFlowLogGroup.Arn}:*'

  BackboneVpcFlowLog:
    Type: AWS::EC2::FlowLog
    Properties:
      DeliverLogsPermissionArn: !GetAtt BackboneFlowLogRole.Arn
      LogDestinationType: cloud-watch-logs
      LogGroupName: !Ref BackboneFlowLogGroup
      ResourceId: !Ref BackboneVpc
      ResourceType: VPC
      TrafficType: ALL

  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-igw-backbone'

  VpcIgwAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref BackboneVpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway

  BackboneRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref BackboneVpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-rt-backbone'

  DefaultRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: VpcIgwAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref BackboneRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway

  BackboneSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref BackboneVpc
      CidrBlock: !Ref BackboneSubnetCidr
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-sn-backbone'

  SubnetRouteAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref BackboneSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref BackboneRouteTable

  BackboneSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: AWS backbone security group for OCI hybrid interconnect demos.
      VpcId: !Ref BackboneVpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - Description: Allow approved HTTPS ingress to the backbone edge.
          IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          CidrIp: !Ref AllowedIngressCidr
      SecurityGroupEgress:
        - Description: Allow HTTPS egress toward the OCI backbone CIDR.
          IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          CidrIp: !Ref OciBackboneCidr
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-sg-backbone'

  TransitGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::TransitGateway
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub '${AWS::StackName} transit gateway for OCI backbone interconnect'
      DefaultRouteTableAssociation: enable
      DefaultRouteTablePropagation: enable
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-tgw-backbone'

  TransitGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::TransitGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      TransitGatewayId: !Ref TransitGateway
      VpcId: !Ref BackboneVpc
      SubnetIds:
        - !Ref BackboneSubnet
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-tgw-attach-backbone'

  OciCustomerGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::CustomerGateway
    Condition: EnableSiteToSiteVpnCondition
    Properties:
      Type: ipsec.1
      IpAddress: !Ref OciCustomerGatewayPublicIp
      BgpAsn: !Ref OciBgpAsn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cgw-oci-primary'

  OciSiteToSiteVpnConnection:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPNConnection
    Condition: EnableSiteToSiteVpnCondition
    Properties:
      Type: ipsec.1
      TransitGatewayId: !Ref TransitGateway
      CustomerGatewayId: !Ref OciCustomerGateway
      StaticRoutesOnly: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-vpn-oci-primary'

  BackboneToOciTransitRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Condition: EnableSiteToSiteVpnCondition
    DependsOn:
      - TransitGatewayAttachment
      - OciSiteToSiteVpnConnection
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref BackboneRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: !Ref OciBackboneCidr
      TransitGatewayId: !Ref TransitGateway

Outputs:
  AwsTransitGatewayId:
    Description: Transit Gateway ID for OCI DRG attachment contracts.
    Value: !Ref TransitGateway
  AwsTransitGatewayAttachmentId:
    Description: Transit Gateway attachment ID.
    Value: !Ref TransitGatewayAttachment
  AwsBackboneVpcId:
    Description: AWS backbone VPC ID.
    Value: !Ref BackboneVpc
  AwsBackboneSubnetId:
    Description: AWS backbone subnet ID.
    Value: !Ref BackboneSubnet
  AwsBackboneRouteTableId:
    Description: AWS backbone route table ID.
    Value: !Ref BackboneRouteTable
  AwsBackboneSecurityGroupId:
    Description: AWS backbone security group ID.
    Value: !Ref BackboneSecurityGroup
  AwsCustomerGatewayId:
    Description: AWS Customer Gateway ID for OCI-primary Site-to-Site VPN.
    Value: !If [EnableSiteToSiteVpnCondition, !Ref OciCustomerGateway, ""]
  AwsVpnConnectionId:

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates an automated photo analysis system. Users will upload images to an S3 bucket, and the system will use Amazon Rekognition to detect whether the image contains a human. If a human is found, an SMS notification is sent to a configurable phone number (default "+14070000000"). The workflow should be event-driven: an S3 event triggers a Lambda function that starts a Step Functions state machine. The state machine invokes a Rekognition Lambda to analyze the image, then either notifies via another Lambda that publishes to SNS or passes through if no human is detected. The template must handle the circular dependency between the S3 bucket's event notification configuration and the Lambda permission, ensuring the bucket can trigger the initial Lambda. Output the bucket name for uploading.
ground_truth_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
# This is created from Advanced Developer, without CDK or Cloud9.
# Upload photos into the resulting S3 bucket and it will tell you if it contains a human or not.
# There is an interesting circular-relationship between the bucket and the lambda it fires:
#   1. To fire the lambda, the bucket must have an event notification defined on it.
#   2. For the event notification to be valid, the bucket must have permission to call the lambda.
#   2. The permission must refer to the bucket, but the bucket doesn't exist yet.
# Failing to resolve this gets "Unable to validate the following destination configurations" error on the S3 bucket create.

Parameters:
  NotificationPhoneNumber:
    Description:  Cell Phone / SMS Number to be contacted at.
    Type:  String
    Default:  "+14070000000"

Resources:
  # This role is shared (!) by the rekognition function and human notification function:
  rekRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-rekRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com

  rekognitionPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-rekPolicy
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - rekognition:Get*
              - rekognition:List*
              - rekognition:Describe*
              - rekognition:Detect*
            Resource: "*"
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - sns:Get*
              - sns:List*
              - sns:Publish
            Resource: "*"
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - s3:Get*
              - s3:List*
            Resource: "*"
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - logs:*
            Resource: "*"
      Roles: [!Ref rekRole]

  onS3UploadCallStepFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-onS3UploadCallStepFunctionRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole"

  onS3UploadCallStepFunctionPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-onS3UploadCallStepFunctionPolicy
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: states:StartExecution
            Resource: !Ref StateMachine
      Roles: [ !Ref onS3UploadCallStepFunctionRole ]

  # This role controls what the state machine can do:
  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-stateMachineRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Principal:
              Service: !Sub states.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com

  # The state machine can call these two Lambda functions:
  StateMachinePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub ${AWS::StackName}-StateMachinePolicy
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
            Resource: !GetAtt rekFunction.Arn
          - Effect: Allow
            Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
            Resource: !GetAtt notificationFunction.Arn
      PolicyName: StateMachinePolicy
      Roles: [ !Ref StateMachineRole ]

  #  Bucket into which one can upload images.  If images contain a human, you will be notified.
  UploadBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DependsOn: UploadBucketPermission  # Can't add event successfully unless permissions are first setup.
    Properties:
      NotificationConfiguration:
        LambdaConfigurations:
        - Event: "s3:ObjectCreated:*"
          Function: !GetAtt onS3UploadCallStepFunction.Arn

  # This permission allows a function to be executed by the S3 service's upload bucket:
  UploadBucketPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !Ref onS3UploadCallStepFunction
      Principal: s3.amazonaws.com
      SourceAccount: !Ref "AWS::AccountId"
      # Notice how this source ARN is defined loosely.
      # If we point to the UploadBucket.Arn, but bucket will be build first,
      # but it can't because it's notification will be invalid, error is:
      # "Unable to validate the following destination configurations"
      #  SourceArn: !GetAtt UploadBucket.Arn
      SourceArn: !Sub "arn:aws:s3:::*"  # Intentially loose to get around the circular reference problem.

  # This function fires whenever an object is uploaded to the S3 upload bucket.  It launches StepFunctions.
  onS3UploadCallStepFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Code:
        ZipFile: !Sub |
          # Lambda function to execute Step Function based on s3 event
          import boto3
          import json
          import os

          def handler(event, context):
              print('Initiating image rekognition')
              for record in event['Records']:
                  bucket = record['s3']['bucket']['name']
                  key = record['s3']['object']['key']

              print('Detected the following image in S3')
              print('Bucket: ' + bucket + ' key name: ' + key)
              ourObject = {
                  "ourBucket": bucket,
                  "ourKey": key
                  }
              # Replace Step Function ARN
              stepARN = os.environ['STEP_ARN']
              client = boto3.client('stepfunctions')
              response = client.start_execution(
                  stateMachineArn=stepARN,
                  input = json.dumps(ourObject)
              )
              return
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt onS3UploadCallStepFunctionRole.Arn
      Runtime: python3.11
      Environment:
        Variables:
          STEP_ARN: !Ref StateMachine

  # This Lambda is called by step functions to do image recognition.  It looks for humans in the picture.
  rekFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Code:
        ZipFile: !Sub |
          from __future__ import print_function
          import boto3
          def handler(event, context):
              print('Initiating image rekognition')
              bucket = event['ourBucket']
              key = event['ourKey']
              client = boto3.client('rekognition')
              response = client.detect_labels(Image={'S3Object': {'Bucket':bucket, 'Name':key}},
                  MaxLabels=10,
                  MinConfidence=75)
              print('Detected the following labels for ' + key)
              for label in response['Labels']:
                  labelName = label['Name']
                  print(labelName + ' : ' + str(label['Confidence']))
                  if labelName == "Human" or labelName == "Person":
                      found = 'human'
                      break
                  else:
                      found = 'other'
              discovery = {
                  "found": found,
                  }
              return discovery

      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt rekRole.Arn
      Runtime: python3.11

  # This Lambda is called by step functions when a human is found.
  # It sends an SNS notification - you can't do this directly from Step Functions.
  notificationFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Code:
        ZipFile: !Sub |
          from __future__ import print_function
          import boto3
          import os
          def handler(event, context):
              phoneNumber = os.environ['PHONE_NUMBER']
              smsMessage = "We found a human!"
              print('Initiating image rekognition')
              found = event['found']
              if found == 'human' || found == 'person':
                  sns_client = boto3.client('sns')
                  sms = sns_client.publish(
                      PhoneNumber = phoneNumber,
                      Message= smsMessage,
                  )
              else:
                  raise Exception('No human detected')
              return

      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt rekRole.Arn
      Runtime: python3.11
      Environment:
        Variables:
          PHONE_NUMBER: !Ref NotificationPhoneNumber

  StateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      DefinitionString: !Sub |-
        {
          "StartAt": "Process Image",
          "TimeoutSeconds":300,
          "States": {
            "Process Image": {
              "Next": "Human Found?",
              "Type":"Task",
              "Resource":  "${rekFunction.Arn}"
            },
            "Human Found?":{
              "Type":"Choice",
              "Choices":[
                {"Variable": "$.found", "StringEquals":"human", "Next":"Process Human"},
                {"Variable":"$.found", "StringEquals":"other",   "Next":"Other Processing"}
              ]
            },
            "Process Human":{
              "Next":"We succeeded! Yay!",
              "Type":"Task",
              "Resource": "${notificationFunction.Arn}"
            },
            "Other Processing": {
              "Type":"Pass",
              "Next":"We succeeded! Yay!"
            },
            "We succeeded! Yay!": {
              "Type":"Succeed"
            }
          }
        }
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn

Outputs:
  TheUploadBucket:
    Description:  URL of the S3 Bucket you can upload images to.  If images contain a human you should be notified.
    Value: !Ref UploadBucket

  LogRetention:

      - 3653
    Default: 7
    ConstraintDescription: Select a value.

Mappings:
  TestConfig:
    LambdaFunctions:
      Prefix: LambdaFunctionInvokerHookTest

Resources:
  LambdaFunction1:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: LogGroup1
    Properties:
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          """Contract tests Lambda function called by AWSSamples::LambdaFunctionInvoker::Hook."""

          import logging
          import os

          LOGGER = logging.getLogger()

          LOGGER.setLevel("INFO")
          # LOGGER.setLevel("DEBUG")

          # Define for which invocation points to run. Comment out the line
          # corresponding to the invocation point you do not want to run.
          HOOK_INVOCATION_POINTS = [
              "CREATE_PRE_PROVISION",
              "UPDATE_PRE_PROVISION",
              "DELETE_PRE_PROVISION",
          ]

          # Used for toggling between callback-based workflows or not.
          # For testing purposes only.
          USE_CALLBACKS = os.environ["USE_CALLBACKS"]
          CALLBACK_CONTEXT = {"test": 1}
          CALLBACK_DELAY_SECONDS = 0

          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              """Define the entry point of the function."""
              LOGGER.debug(event)

              request = event["request"]
              invocation_point = request["hookContext"]["invocationPoint"]
              LOGGER.info(f"Invocation point: {invocation_point}")
              if invocation_point not in HOOK_INVOCATION_POINTS:
                  return {
                      "status": "SUCCESS",
                      "errorCode": None,
                      "message": f"Skipping target evaluation for {invocation_point}.",
                      "callbackContext": None,
                      "callbackDelaySeconds": 0,
                  }

              target_model = request["hookContext"]["targetModel"]
              resource_properties = target_model["resourceProperties"]
              LOGGER.debug(f"Resource properties: {resource_properties}")

              callback_context = event["callbackContext"]
              LOGGER.debug(f"Callback context: {callback_context}")

              if callback_context:

By default the scanner Lambda should run outside any VPC, which is the simplest path and only works if the access point being scanned is internet-origin; before invoking, the access point's network origin should be checked and if it comes back as VPC-scoped, the VPC ID, subnet IDs, a security group ID, and route table IDs must be supplied so the Lambda can be deployed inside that same VPC to reach it, since these all default to empty for the outside-VPC case. When a VPC ID is supplied, the template should optionally create the VPC endpoints needed for the Lambda to reach S3, DynamoDB, Comprehend, and SNS, controlled by a create-endpoints flag that defaults to true; this flag should be set to false instead if the target VPC already has any of those four endpoints, since a duplicate Interface endpoint for a service that already has one, or a second S3 Gateway endpoint bound to the same route tables, will fail and roll back the whole stack. The template should include a DynamoDB table for classification reports with point-in-time recovery and encryption, an IAM role granting the Lambda permissions to read from the access point, call Comprehend, write to DynamoDB, publish to SNS, and create logs, and a Lambda function with configurable memory (defaulting to 512 MB), timeout (defaulting to 600 seconds), a default Comprehend language code (defaulting to English), and a default maximum number of files to scan per invocation (defaulting to 500, as a cost and runtime control). The Lambda code should handle chunking of large files, sampling, and pagination through the access point's objects. The stack should output the scanner function ARN, the report table name, and an example CLI invocation command.

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  FSx for ONTAP Content-Level PII Classification Scanner (CSF 2.0 Identify).
  Scans files via an S3 Access Point using Amazon Comprehend
  DetectPiiEntities. QUICK START: leave VpcId empty to deploy outside any
  VPC — this is the simplest path and requires only an internet-origin S3
  Access Point (check with `aws s3control get-access-point --account-id
  <id> --name <ap-name> --query NetworkOrigin`; "Internet" works with the
  default parameters below, "VPC" requires setting VpcId/SubnetIds/
  SecurityGroupId/RouteTableIds to the VPC the access point is bound to).
  No FSx control-plane API calls are made by this stack, so it has no
  dependency on any FSx Interface VPC Endpoint even when VpcId is set.
  Stack name pattern: fsxn-content-classification

Parameters:
  VpcId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      VPC ID to run the scanner Lambda inside. Leave empty (default) to
      deploy outside any VPC — the simplest path, and the only requirement
      is that the access_point_arn you invoke with is an Internet-origin
      S3 Access Point (verify with `aws s3control get-access-point
      --account-id <account-id> --name <ap-name> --query NetworkOrigin`).
      Set this ONLY if the access_point_arn you plan to scan is VPC-scoped
      (NetworkOrigin=VPC, e.g., one created by restore-verification.yaml's
      AttachAccessPoint step) — a VPC-scoped access point has no route from
      outside its bound VPC, so the Lambda must run inside that same VPC.
      When set, also set SubnetIds/SecurityGroupId/RouteTableIds below to
      match that VPC.
    Default: ''
    AllowedPattern: '^(vpc-[0-9a-f]{8,17})?$'

  SubnetIds:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Description: >-
      Private subnet IDs for the scanner Lambda. Required if VpcId is set;
      ignored otherwise. Leave as the default single empty-string entry
      when VpcId is empty.
    Default: ''

  SecurityGroupId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Security Group ID for the scanner Lambda (egress to VPC Endpoints).
      Required if VpcId is set; ignored otherwise.
    Default: ''
    AllowedPattern: '^(sg-[0-9a-f]{8,17})?$'

  RouteTableIds:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Description: >-
      Route table IDs associated with SubnetIds. Used to attach the S3 and
      DynamoDB Gateway VPC Endpoints the scanner needs when running inside
      a VPC. Required if VpcId is set and CreateVpcEndpoints=true; ignored
      otherwise.
    Default: ''

  CreateVpcEndpoints:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      When VpcId is set, create VPC Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB (Gateway)
      plus Comprehend and SNS (Interface) so the in-VPC scanner Lambda can
      reach the access point, report table, PII detection API, and
      notifications. Set to 'false' if your VPC already has all four —
      check first with `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters

      and rolls back this whole stack). If reusing restore-verification.
      yaml's VPC: that stack creates Secrets Manager/STS/FSx/S3-Gateway
      endpoints, none of which overlap with this stack's Comprehend/
      DynamoDB/SNS/S3-Gateway set except S3 — if that stack's
      CreateS3GatewayEndpoint was 'true', check for that existing S3
      Gateway Endpoint before setting this to 'true' (a second S3 Gateway
      Endpoint bound to the same route tables is rejected as a duplicate).
      Ignored if VpcId is empty.
    Default: 'true'
    AllowedValues: ['true', 'false']

  LambdaMemorySize:
    Type: Number
    Description: Lambda memory size in MB for the scanner function
    Default: 512
    AllowedValues: [256, 512, 1024, 2048]

  LambdaTimeoutSeconds:
    Type: Number

      Lambda timeout in seconds. Scanning many/large files against
      Comprehend can take time — size this to your expected file count.
    Default: 600
    MinValue: 60
    MaxValue: 900

  DefaultLanguageCode:
    Type: String

    Default: en

    Type: Number

    Default: 500

  NotificationTopicArn:

Conditions:
  HasNotificationTopic: !Not [!Equals [!Ref NotificationTopicArn, '']]
  HasVpc: !Not [!Equals [!Ref VpcId, '']]
  ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints: !And
    - !Condition HasVpc
    - !Equals [!Ref CreateVpcEndpoints, 'true']

Resources:
  # ================================================================
  # VPC Endpoints — only created when VpcId is set and
  # CreateVpcEndpoints=true. Required so the in-VPC scanner Lambda can
  # reach: the VPC-scoped S3 Access Point being scanned (S3 Gateway), the
  # DynamoDB report table (DynamoDB Gateway), Comprehend DetectPiiEntities
  # (Comprehend Interface), and SNS notifications (SNS Interface).
  # ================================================================
  S3GatewayVpcEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.s3'
      VpcEndpointType: Gateway
      RouteTableIds: !Ref RouteTableIds

  DynamoDbGatewayVpcEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.dynamodb'
      VpcEndpointType: Gateway
      RouteTableIds: !Ref RouteTableIds

  ComprehendVpcEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.comprehend'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      SubnetIds: !Ref SubnetIds
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true

  SnsVpcEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.sns'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      SubnetIds: !Ref SubnetIds
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true

  VpcEndpointSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Allow scanner Lambda to access Interface VPC Endpoints (Comprehend, SNS)
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref SecurityGroupId
          Description: Lambda SG to VPC Endpoint (HTTPS)

  # ================================================================
  # DynamoDB — classification report ledger
  # ================================================================
  ClassificationReportTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-reports'
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: access_point_arn
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: started_at
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: access_point_arn
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: started_at
          KeyType: RANGE
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: fsxn-observability
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: content-classification-report

  # ================================================================
  # Lambda Execution Role
  # ================================================================
  ScannerLambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-lambda-role'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      # Attached unconditionally — harmless when VpcId is empty (the
      # scanner Lambda simply won't have ENIs to manage), and avoids a
      # Fn::If on ManagedPolicyArns.
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ContentClassificationPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: S3AccessPointObjectRead
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:ListBucket
                  - s3:GetObject
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:accesspoint/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:accesspoint/*/object/*'
              - Sid: ComprehendDetectPii
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - comprehend:DetectPiiEntities
                Resource: '*'
                # DetectPiiEntities does not support resource-level
                # permissions (it is a synchronous, stateless inference
                # API with no addressable resource).
              - Sid: DynamoDbReportLedger
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - dynamodb:PutItem
                Resource: !GetAtt ClassificationReportTable.Arn
              - Sid: SNSPublish
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - sns:Publish
                Resource: !If
                  - HasNotificationTopic
                  - !Ref NotificationTopicArn
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:sns:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:*'
              - Sid: CloudWatchLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-scanner:*'

  ScannerLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-scanner'
      RetentionInDays: 365  # classification reports double as CSF 2.0 Identify evidence

  # ================================================================
  # Lambda — Content Classification Scanner
  # ================================================================
  ScannerFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-scanner'
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      MemorySize: !Ref LambdaMemorySize
      Timeout: !Ref LambdaTimeoutSeconds
      Role: !GetAtt ScannerLambdaRole.Arn
      # Only set VpcConfig when VpcId is provided. A VPC-scoped S3 Access
      # Point (e.g., from restore-verification.yaml's AttachAccessPoint
      # step) has no route from outside its bound VPC, so scanning one
      # requires this Lambda to run inside that VPC — see the Description
      # above and Security Considerations in content-classification-scanner.md.
      VpcConfig: !If
        - HasVpc
        - SubnetIds: !Ref SubnetIds
          SecurityGroupIds:
            - !Ref SecurityGroupId
        - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'
      Environment:
        Variables:
          REPORT_TABLE_NAME: !Ref ClassificationReportTable
          DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_CODE: !Ref DefaultLanguageCode
          DEFAULT_MAX_FILES: !Ref DefaultMaxFiles
          NOTIFICATION_TOPIC_ARN: !If [HasNotificationTopic, !Ref NotificationTopicArn, '']
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          """Content-level PII discovery scanner (CSF 2.0 Identify function).

          Invocation input (direct Lambda invoke or Step Functions task):
          {
              "access_point_arn": "arn:aws:s3:...:accesspoint/...",  // required
              "language_code": "en",                                  // optional
              "max_files": 500                                        // optional
          }

          Scans scannable text/structured-data files exposed via the given
          S3 Access Point for PII entities using Amazon Comprehend
          DetectPiiEntities, aggregates findings, writes a report to
          DynamoDB, and optionally notifies via SNS.

          Does NOT create or manage the S3 Access Point itself — pass the
          ARN of an existing one (e.g., from restore-verification.yaml's
          AttachAccessPoint step, or any other FSx for ONTAP S3 Access Point
          you want to classify).
          """
          import json
          import logging
          import os
          from dataclasses import dataclass, field
          from datetime import datetime, timezone
          from typing import Any

          import boto3
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

          s3 = boto3.client("s3")
          comprehend = boto3.client("comprehend")
          dynamodb = boto3.resource("dynamodb")
          sns = boto3.client("sns")

          COMPREHEND_MAX_BYTES = 100_000
          CHUNK_SAFETY_MARGIN_BYTES = 2_000
          CHUNK_TARGET_BYTES = COMPREHEND_MAX_BYTES - CHUNK_SAFETY_MARGIN_BYTES

          SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS = frozenset({
              ".txt", ".csv", ".tsv", ".json", ".xml", ".log", ".md",
              ".yaml", ".yml", ".ini", ".conf", ".sql", ".html", ".htm",
          })

          DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_BYTES = 5_000_000
          DEFAULT_SAMPLE_BYTES = 500_000

          COMPREHEND_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES = frozenset({
              "en", "es", "fr", "de", "it", "pt", "ar", "hi", "ja", "ko", "zh", "zh-TW",
          })

          def _chunk_text(text, target_bytes=CHUNK_TARGET_BYTES):
              if not text:
                  return []
              chunks = []
              current_lines, current_bytes = [], 0
              for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
                  line_bytes = len(line.encode("utf-8"))
                  if line_bytes > target_bytes:
                      if current_lines:
                          chunks.append("".join(current_lines))
                          current_lines, current_bytes = [], 0
                      encoded = line.encode("utf-8")
                      for i in range(0, len(encoded), target_bytes):
                          chunks.append(encoded[i:i + target_bytes].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
                      continue
                  if current_bytes + line_bytes > target_bytes and current_lines:
                      chunks.append("".join(current_lines))
                      current_lines, current_bytes = [], 0
                  current_lines.append(line)
                  current_bytes += line_bytes
              if current_lines:
                  chunks.append("".join(current_lines))
              return chunks

          def _classify_object(access_point_arn, key, size_bytes, language_code):
              sampled = size_bytes > DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_BYTES
              finding = {"key": key, "size_bytes": size_bytes, "sampled": sampled,
                         "entity_counts": {}, "highest_confidence_by_type": {}, "error": ""}

              try:
                  if sampled:
                      resp = s3.get_object(Bucket=access_point_arn, Key=key,
                                           Range=f"bytes=0-{DEFAULT_SAMPLE_BYTES - 1}")
                  else:
                      resp = s3.get_object(Bucket=access_point_arn, Key=key)
                  raw = resp["Body"].read()
              except ClientError as e:
                  finding["error"] = f"read_failed: {e}"
                  return finding

              text = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
              if not text.strip():
                  return finding

              for chunk in _chunk_text(text):
                  if not chunk.strip():
                      continue
                  try:
                      resp = comprehend.detect_pii_entities(Text=chunk, LanguageCode=language_code)
                  except ClientError as e:
                      finding["error"] = f"comprehend_failed: {e}"
                      continue
                  for entity in resp.get("Entities", []):
                      etype = entity.get("Type", "UNKNOWN")
                      score = entity.get("Score", 0.0)
                      finding["entity_counts"][etype] = finding["entity_counts"].get(etype, 0) + 1
                      finding["highest_confidence_by_type"][etype] = max(
                          finding["highest_confidence_by_type"].get(etype, 0.0), score
                      )

              return finding

          def lambda_handler(event: dict[str, Any], context: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
              access_point_arn = event["access_point_arn"]
              language_code = event.get("language_code", os.environ.get("DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_CODE", "en"))
              max_files = int(event.get("max_files", os.environ.get("DEFAULT_MAX_FILES", "500")))

              if language_code not in COMPREHEND_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES:
                  raise ValueError(
                      f"Unsupported language_code '{language_code}' — must be one of "
                      f"{sorted(COMPREHEND_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES)}"
                  )

              started_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
              files_scanned = 0
              files_skipped_unscannable = 0
              files_sampled_too_large = 0
              files_with_pii = 0
              pii_density_by_type = {}
              findings = []

              paginator = s3.get_paginator("list_objects_v2")
              for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=access_point_arn, MaxKeys=1000):
                  for obj in page.get("Contents", []):
                      if files_scanned >= max_files:
                          break
                      key = obj["Key"]
                      size_bytes = obj.get("Size", 0)
                      lower_key = key.lower()

                      if not any(lower_key.endswith(ext) for ext in SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS):
                          files_skipped_unscannable += 1
                          continue
                      if size_bytes == 0:
                          continue

                      finding = _classify_object(access_point_arn, key, size_bytes, language_code)
                      files_scanned += 1

                      if finding["sampled"]:
                          files_sampled_too_large += 1
                      if finding["entity_counts"]:
                          files_with_pii += 1
                          findings.append(finding)
                          for etype, count in finding["entity_counts"].items():
                              pii_density_by_type[etype] = pii_density_by_type.get(etype, 0) + count
                      elif finding["error"]:
                          findings.append(finding)
                  if files_scanned >= max_files:
                      break

              completed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
              report = {
                  "access_point_arn": access_point_arn,
                  "started_at": started_at,
                  "completed_at": completed_at,
                  "language_code": language_code,
                  "files_scanned": files_scanned,
                  "files_skipped_unscannable": files_skipped_unscannable,
                  "files_sampled_too_large": files_sampled_too_large,
                  "files_with_pii": files_with_pii,
                  "pii_density_by_type": pii_density_by_type,
                  "findings": findings[:100],
                  "finding_count": len(findings),
              }

              table = dynamodb.Table(os.environ["REPORT_TABLE_NAME"])
              table.put_item(Item=json.loads(json.dumps(report), parse_float=str))

              logger.info(
                  "Classification complete: %d files scanned, %d with PII, %d unscannable skipped",
                  files_scanned, files_with_pii, files_skipped_unscannable,
              )

              topic_arn = os.environ.get("NOTIFICATION_TOPIC_ARN")
              if topic_arn and files_with_pii > 0:
                  try:
                      sns.publish(
                          TopicArn=topic_arn,
                          Subject=f"[FSx-ONTAP PII Scan] {files_with_pii} file(s) with PII found"[:100],
                          Message=json.dumps(
                              {k: v for k, v in report.items() if k != "findings"},
                              indent=2, default=str,
                          ),
                      )
                  except Exception as e:
                      logger.warning("Notification failed: %s", e)

              return report

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates two separate Cognito authentication setups for a PiBot project: one for the main web application and one for IoT trusted user provisioning. The provisioning setup should similarly include a user pool, client, identity pool, and roles, but the authenticated role should instead grant permissions for IoT trusted user provisioning actions. Both identity pools should be attached to their respective roles, and the template should output the identity pool IDs, user pool IDs, and client IDs for both setups.

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: 2010-09-09
Transform: 'AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31'
Resources:
  #######################
  # IAM Roles

  # Cognito for PiBot Web application
  cognitoAuthRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role

      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Effect: "Allow"
            Principal:
              Federated: 'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com'
            Action:
              - 'sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                "cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud": !Ref PibotIDPool

      Path: '/'
      Policies:

            Version: "2012-10-17"

                  - "mobileanalytics:PutEvents"
                  - "cognito-sync:*"
                  - "cognito-identity:*"
                Resource: "*"
        - PolicyName: "iot-access"

            Version: "2012-10-17"

              - Effect: "Allow"

                  - "kinesisvideo:Get*"
                  - "kinesisvideo:List*"
                  - "rekognition:DetectLabels"

  cognitoUnauthRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role

              - 'sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity'

    Properties:

        unauthenticated: !GetAtt cognitoProvUnauthRole.Arn
        authenticated: !GetAtt cognitoProvAuthRole.Arn

    Value: !Ref PibotIDPool

    Value: !Ref PiBotUserPool
  cognitoClientIdweb:
    Description: 'UserPool client ID for the main web app'
    Value: !Ref PibotUserPoolClient
  cognitoIdPoolIdprov:

  cognitoUserPoolprov:
    Description: 'UserPool Pool ID for Cognito auth for the Trusted User Provisioning web app'
    Value: !Ref ProvisioningUserPool
  cognitoClientIdprov:
    Description: 'UserPool client ID for the Trusted User Provisioning web app'
    Value: !Ref ProvisioningUserPoolClient
