The template should not provision the backend compute or authentication providers; instead, it must dynamically resolve existing configuration from SSM Parameter Store. Create an IAM role for the 'bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com' service that grants permission to invoke a Lambda function (retrieving the Lambda ARN dynamically from SSM) and store this new IAM role's ARN in a standard SSM parameter. Provision the AgentCore Gateway configured with a custom JWT authorizer that dynamically references a Cognito discovery URL and client ID from SSM. Next, create a gateway target connecting the gateway to the Lambda function, defining an MCP inline tool schema with 'invoke_endpoint' and 'get_results' operations for submitting sequences and checking job completion. Include parameters for the project name (defaulting to 'protein-engineering'), gateway description, and an optional gateway name that auto-generates from the project name if left blank.
ground_truth_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'Gateway Stack - Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway infrastructure for MCP integration'

# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE OVERVIEW
# ============================================================================
# This CloudFormation template deploys Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
# with MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for AI agent communication.
#
# Key Components:
# - IAM Role for AgentCore Gateway with Lambda invoke permissions
# - AgentCore Gateway with JWT authorization (Cognito integration)
# - Gateway Target connecting to Lambda function for protein prediction
# - MCP tool schema defining invoke_endpoint and get_results operations
#
# Dependencies:
# - VEP Stack: Requires Lambda function ARN from SSM Parameter Store
# - Cognito Stack: Requires discovery URL and client ID from SSM Parameter Store
#
# Stack Deployment Order:
# 1. VEP Endpoint Stack (creates Lambda, stores ARN in SSM)
# 2. Cognito Stack (creates auth config, stores in SSM)
# 3. Gateway Stack (reads from SSM, creates gateway) <- THIS STACK
#
# Outputs:
# - Gateway URL for MCP client connections
# - Gateway ID and ARN for reference
# - IAM role information
# ============================================================================

Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: 'Project Configuration'
        Parameters:
          - ProjectName
      - Label:
          default: 'Gateway Configuration'
        Parameters:
          - GatewayName
          - GatewayDescription
    ParameterLabels:
      ProjectName:
        default: 'Project Name'
      GatewayName:
        default: 'Gateway Name'
      GatewayDescription:
        default: 'Gateway Description'

# ============================================================================
# PARAMETERS
# ============================================================================
# Configure Gateway naming and description
# ============================================================================

Parameters:
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Project Configuration
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ProjectName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'protein-engineering'
    Description: 'Project name used for resource naming and tagging'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: 'Must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens'

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gateway Configuration
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  GatewayName:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: 'Name for the AgentCore Gateway (leave empty to auto-generate from project name)'
    MaxLength: 128
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]*$'
    ConstraintDescription: 'Must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores'

  GatewayDescription:
    Type: String
    Default: 'AgentCore Gateway for protein engineering agent with MCP integration'
    Description: 'Description for the AgentCore Gateway'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 256

# ============================================================================
# CONDITIONS
# ============================================================================
Conditions:
  UseGeneratedGatewayName: !Equals [!Ref GatewayName, '']

# ============================================================================
# RESOURCES
# ============================================================================
Resources:
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # PLACEHOLDER VALUES (was a self-containment gap on a separate VEP Endpoint
  # stack and Cognito stack, see TEMPLATE OVERVIEW above). First fix stubbed
  # these via AWS::SSM::Parameter + {{resolve:ssm:...}} dynamic references,
  # but that failed on real AWS with a stack-level "no StackStatusReason or
  # FAILED resource event found" error: CloudFormation resolves dynamic
  # references during an early template-processing pass that does not
  # reliably honor DependsOn against a parameter created earlier in the SAME
  # template (confirmed via CloudTrail -- the stack failed before the SSM
  # ssm:PutParameter call for these resources ever happened). Since these
  # were only ever placeholder/non-secret values anyway, inlined them as
  # plain literals instead -- no dynamic reference, no ordering hazard.
  #
  # The Cognito discovery URL could NOT stay a fake string: AgentCore Gateway
  # creation actually HTTP-fetches AuthorizerConfiguration's DiscoveryUrl to
  # build the JWT authorizer, so a placeholder domain fails with "Failed to
  # fetch discovery document" (confirmed on a real deploy attempt). Fixed by
  # creating a real (empty, unused) Cognito User Pool + Client below -- every
  # real User Pool automatically serves a working OIDC discovery document at
  # this well-known path, no Domain/UI needed for that.
  #
  # UPDATE: the Lambda ARN placeholder turned out to need the same treatment,
  # contradicting the assumption above -- AWS::BedrockAgentCore::GatewayTarget
  # also actively validates its target at creation time (confirmed on a real
  # deploy attempt: "Lambda function not found: ...protein-agent-placeholder").
  # Replaced the bare ARN string with a real, minimal Lambda function stub
  # below (same "trivial stub preserves the scenario's intent, not the real
  # function body" precedent used throughout this benchmark) instead of
  # continuing to assume an unvalidated placeholder is safe.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ProteinAgentPlaceholderExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${ProjectName}-protein-agent-placeholder-role'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        - Key: Component
          Value: Gateway

  ProteinAgentPlaceholderFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: protein-agent-placeholder
      Description: 'Minimal stub target for the AgentCore GatewayTarget (invoke_endpoint / get_results) -- exercises the Gateway wiring, not the real prediction logic'
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt ProteinAgentPlaceholderExecutionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 10
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          def handler(event, context):
              return {"output_id": "stub-output-id", "status": "COMPLETED", "result": {}}
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        - Key: Component
          Value: Gateway

  PlaceholderUserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: !Sub '${ProjectName}-gateway-placeholder-pool'

  PlaceholderUserPoolClient:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Sub '${ProjectName}-gateway-placeholder-client'
      UserPoolId: !Ref PlaceholderUserPool
      GenerateSecret: false

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM ROLE FOR AGENTCORE GATEWAY
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Allows Gateway to invoke Lambda function for protein prediction
  # Uses dynamic SSM reference to get Lambda ARN from VEP stack
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  GatewayRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    # Purpose: Grants AgentCore Gateway permission to invoke Lambda function
    # Trust Policy: Only bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com can assume this role
    # Conditions: Restricts to same account and AgentCore service ARNs
    # Permissions: lambda:InvokeFunction on the placeholder Lambda ARN below
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${ProjectName}-agentcore-gateway-role'
      Description: 'Execution role for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to invoke Lambda functions'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref AWS::AccountId
              ArnLike:
                'aws:SourceArn': !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:bedrock-agentcore:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: 'LambdaInvokeAccess'
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'lambda:InvokeFunction'
                Resource: !GetAtt ProteinAgentPlaceholderFunction.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        - Key: Component
          Value: Gateway
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SSM PARAMETER FOR GATEWAY ROLE
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Stores Gateway role ARN for reference (optional, for future use)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  GatewayRoleArnParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    # Purpose: Stores Gateway IAM role ARN for reference
    # Usage: Can be used by monitoring or management tools
    Properties:
      Name: '/protein-agent/gateway/role-arn'
      Description: 'AgentCore Gateway IAM role ARN'
      Type: String
      Value: !GetAtt GatewayRole.Arn
      Tier: Standard
      Tags:
        Project: !Ref ProjectName
        ManagedBy: CloudFormation

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AGENTCORE GATEWAY
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Main gateway resource that provides MCP endpoint for AI agents
  # Configured with JWT authorization using Cognito
  # Uses dynamic SSM references to retrieve Cognito configuration
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  AgentCoreGateway:
    Type: AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Gateway
    # Purpose: Creates MCP-compatible gateway for AI agent communication
    # Protocol: MCP (Model Context Protocol) with SEMANTIC search
    # Authorization: CUSTOM_JWT using Cognito for token validation
    Properties:
      Name: !If [UseGeneratedGatewayName, !Sub '${ProjectName}-gateway', !Ref GatewayName]
      Description: !Ref GatewayDescription
      RoleArn: !GetAtt GatewayRole.Arn
      ProtocolType: MCP
      AuthorizerType: CUSTOM_JWT
      AuthorizerConfiguration:
        CustomJWTAuthorizer:
          DiscoveryUrl: !Sub 'https://cognito-idp.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${PlaceholderUserPool}/.well-known/openid-configuration'
          AllowedClients:
            - !Ref PlaceholderUserPoolClient
      ProtocolConfiguration:
        Mcp:
          SearchType: SEMANTIC
      Tags:
        Project: !Ref ProjectName
        Component: Gateway
        ManagedBy: CloudFormation

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # GATEWAY TARGET
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Connects Gateway to Lambda function with MCP tool schema
  # Defines invoke_endpoint and get_results operations
  # Uses dynamic SSM reference to retrieve Lambda ARN from VEP stack
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  GatewayTarget:
    Type: AWS::BedrockAgentCore::GatewayTarget
    # Purpose: Connects Gateway to Lambda function for protein prediction
    # Tool Schema: Defines two MCP tools (invoke_endpoint, get_results)
    # Credentials: Uses Gateway IAM role for Lambda invocation
    Properties:
      Name: 'protein-engineering-lambda'
      Description: 'Lambda target for protein variant effect prediction'
      GatewayIdentifier: !Ref AgentCoreGateway
      TargetConfiguration:
        Mcp:
          Lambda:
            LambdaArn: !GetAtt ProteinAgentPlaceholderFunction.Arn
            ToolSchema:
              InlinePayload:
                - Name: 'invoke_endpoint'
                  Description: 'Submit a job to predict the variant effects for an amino acid sequence'
                  InputSchema:
                    Type: 'object'
                    Properties:
                      sequence:
                        Type: 'string'
                        Description: 'Amino acid sequence'
                    Required:
                      - 'sequence'
                - Name: 'get_results'
                  Description: 'Check if a variant effect prediction job has completed and retrieve results'
                  InputSchema:
                    Type: 'object'
                    Properties:
                      output_id:
                        Type: 'string'
                        Description: 'output_id returned by invoke_endpoint'
                    Required:
                      - 'output_id'
      CredentialProviderConfigurations:
        - CredentialProviderType: GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE

# ============================================================================
# OUTPUTS
# ============================================================================
# Provides Gateway connection information and resource identifiers
# ============================================================================

Outputs:
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gateway Outputs
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  GatewayId:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway ID'
    Value: !Ref AgentCoreGateway
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayId'

  GatewayUrl:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway MCP URL'
    Value: !GetAtt AgentCoreGateway.GatewayUrl
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayUrl'

  GatewayArn:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway ARN'
    Value: !GetAtt AgentCoreGateway.GatewayArn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayArn'

  # IAM Role Outputs
  GatewayRoleArn:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway IAM role ARN'
    Value: !GetAtt GatewayRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayRoleArn'

  GatewayRoleName:
    Description: 'AgentCore Gateway IAM role name'
    Value: !Ref GatewayRole
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayRoleName'

  # Target Outputs
  TargetId:
    Description: 'Gateway Target ID'
    Value: !Ref GatewayTarget
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TargetId'

  TargetName:
    Description: 'Gateway Target name'
    Value: 'protein-engineering-lambda'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TargetName'

  # SSM Parameter Outputs
  GatewayRoleArnParameterName:
    Description: 'SSM Parameter name for Gateway role ARN'
    Value: '/protein-agent/gateway/role-arn'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayRoleArnParameter'

  # Configuration Outputs
  ProjectName:
    Description: 'Project name used for resource naming'
    Value: !Ref ProjectName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ProjectName'

  GatewayName:
    Description: 'Gateway name'
    Value: !If [UseGeneratedGatewayName, !Sub '${ProjectName}-gateway', !Ref GatewayName]
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GatewayName'

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a private VPC infrastructure for deploying applications in a secured network. The template should create a VPC with three private subnets spanning multiple availability zones—two subnets for an Application Load Balancer in different AZs as required by ALB, and one separate subnet for Lambda functions. Include support for optional internet egress via a NAT Gateway (enabled or disabled by parameter) to support OAuth and external identity provider flows. Create a customer-managed KMS key for encrypting an artifact storage bucket, with a deletion policy set to Retain so the key persists even after stack deletion. Include DNS support for the VPC and use the provided CIDR parameters for the VPC and each subnet.
ground_truth_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >
  Test VPC for IDP ALB Hosting - Simulates a customer's private network with
  2 private subnets for the ALB (different AZs), 1 additional Lambda subnet
  (for testing private AppSync VPC config), and a standalone KMS CMK for
  artifact bucket encryption.
  The KMS key has DeletionPolicy=Retain so it survives stack deletion.

  Optionally creates an Internet Gateway + NAT Gateway to simulate a
  Direct Connect customer whose private network has routable internet
  egress (required for External IdP / OAuth redirect flows).

  NOTE: This template does NOT create an ACM certificate. Use
  scripts/generate_self_signed_cert.sh after deploying the IDP stack to
  generate a cert that covers the actual ALB DNS hostname. See
  docs/deployment-private-network.md for the 2-step cert process.

Parameters:
  VpcCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.1.0.0/16'
    Description: CIDR block for the VPC

  PrivateSubnet1Cidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.1.1.0/24'
    Description: CIDR block for private subnet 1

  PrivateSubnet2Cidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.1.2.0/24'
    Description: CIDR block for private subnet 2

  LambdaSubnetCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.1.3.0/24'
    Description: CIDR block for the Lambda subnet (separate from ALB subnets)

  EnableNATGateway:
    Type: String
    Default: 'true'
    AllowedValues:
      - 'true'
      - 'false'
    Description: >-
      Create an Internet Gateway + NAT Gateway to provide internet egress
      from private subnets. Set to 'true' to simulate a Direct Connect
      customer with routable internet (required for External IdP/OAuth).
      Set to 'false' for a fully air-gapped VPC (Cognito-only auth via
      PrivateLink — requires deleting the Cognito domain post-deploy).

  PublicSubnetCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.1.5.0/28'
    Description: >-
      CIDR block for the public subnet (hosts the NAT Gateway).
      Only used when EnableNATGateway is true. A /28 is sufficient
      (only needs 1 IP for the NAT Gateway ENI).

Conditions:
  CreateNATGateway: !Equals [ !Ref EnableNATGateway, 'true' ]

Resources:
  #############################################
  # VPC
  #############################################
  VPC:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    # checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_178: "VPC flow logs are not required for this test-only template. Enable flow logs in production VPCs."
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: !Ref VpcCidr
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-TestVPC

  #############################################
  # Private Subnets for ALB (2 AZs required by ALB)
  #############################################
  PrivateSubnet1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      CidrBlock: !Ref PrivateSubnet1Cidr
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-PrivateSubnet1

  PrivateSubnet2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      CidrBlock: !Ref PrivateSubnet2Cidr
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-PrivateSubnet2

  #############################################
  # Lambda Subnet (separate from ALB subnets —
  # used to test IDP Lambdas in a different subnet,
  # e.g. for private AppSync VPC config testing)
  #############################################
  LambdaSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      CidrBlock: !Ref LambdaSubnetCidr
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-LambdaSubnet

  #############################################
  # Route Table for Private Subnets
  #############################################
  PrivateRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-PrivateRouteTable

  PrivateSubnet1RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnet1
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable

  PrivateSubnet2RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnet2
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable

  LambdaSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref LambdaSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable

  #############################################
  # Internet Gateway (conditional — Direct Connect simulation)
  #############################################
  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-IGW

  InternetGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway

  #############################################
  # Public Subnet for NAT Gateway (conditional)
  #############################################
  PublicSubnet:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      CidrBlock: !Ref PublicSubnetCidr
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-PublicSubnet-NAT

  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-PublicRouteTable

  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    DependsOn: InternetGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: '0.0.0.0/0'
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway

  PublicSubnetRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable

  #############################################
  # NAT Gateway + Elastic IP (conditional)
  #############################################
  NATGatewayEIP:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-NAT-EIP

  NATGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NATGatewayEIP.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: IDP-ALB-NATGateway

  #############################################
  # Private route to NAT Gateway (conditional)
  # Provides internet egress for private subnets
  #############################################
  PrivateRouteToNAT:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: '0.0.0.0/0'
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NATGateway

  #############################################
  # KMS CMK for artifact bucket encryption
  # Managed by THIS stack (not the IDP stack) so that
  # deleting the IDP stack never schedules this key for deletion.
  #############################################
  ArtifactBucketKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Metadata:
      cfn_nag:
        rules_to_suppress:
          - id: W79
            reason: "KMS key policy grants kms:* to the account root principal — standard administrative access pattern for CMKs. This test key is intentionally managed outside the IDP stack so deleting the IDP stack does not schedule key deletion."
    # checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_7: "Key rotation is already enabled via EnableKeyRotation: true"
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'CMK for IDP artifact bucket encryption — managed by ${AWS::StackName}'
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAccountRootFullControl
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowS3ServiceUse
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: s3.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - kms:GenerateDataKey
              - kms:Decrypt
            Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ArtifactBucketKey'
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  ArtifactBucketKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: !Sub 'alias/${AWS::StackName}-artifact-bucket-key'
      TargetKeyId: !Ref ArtifactBucketKey

Outputs:
  VpcId:
    Description: VPC ID for IDP ALB deployment
    Value: !Ref VPC
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-VpcId'

  SubnetIds:
    Description: Comma-separated ALB subnet IDs for IDP ALB deployment
    Value: !Sub '${PrivateSubnet1},${PrivateSubnet2}'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-SubnetIds'

  PrivateSubnet1Id:
    Description: Private Subnet 1 ID (ALB)
    Value: !Ref PrivateSubnet1

  PrivateSubnet2Id:
    Description: Private Subnet 2 ID (ALB)
    Value: !Ref PrivateSubnet2

  LambdaSubnetId:
    Description: >
      Lambda subnet ID — use as LambdaSubnetIds when deploying with
      AppSyncVisibility=PRIVATE. Kept separate from ALB subnets so Lambda
      VpcConfig and ALB listeners use different subnets.
    Value: !Ref LambdaSubnet
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-LambdaSubnetId'

  PrivateRouteTableId:
    Description: >-
      Route table ID for private subnets — pass to deploy-vpc-endpoints.py
      --route-table-ids for S3/DynamoDB Gateway endpoints.
    Value: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-PrivateRouteTableId'

  ArtifactBucketKeyArn:
    Description: >
      KMS CMK ARN for artifact bucket encryption — pass as --kms-key-arn
      to publish.py. This key is managed by this stack (NOT the IDP stack),
      so deleting the IDP stack will NOT delete this key.
    Value: !GetAtt ArtifactBucketKey.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ArtifactBucketKeyArn'

  ArtifactBucketKeyAlias:
    Description: KMS CMK alias for artifact bucket encryption
    Value: !Sub 'alias/${AWS::StackName}-artifact-bucket-key'

  InternetGatewayId:
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Description: Internet Gateway ID (only when EnableNATGateway=true)
    Value: !Ref InternetGateway

  NATGatewayId:
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Description: NAT Gateway ID (only when EnableNATGateway=true)
    Value: !Ref NATGateway

  PublicSubnetId:
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Description: Public subnet hosting the NAT Gateway
    Value: !Ref PublicSubnet

  NetworkMode:
    Description: >-
      Indicates whether the VPC has internet egress (Direct Connect simulation)
      or is fully air-gapped. Determines authentication configuration — see
      docs/deployment-private-network.md Step 3.5.
    Value: !If
      - CreateNATGateway
      - "NAT-GATEWAY (internet egress via NAT — supports External IdP)"
      - "AIR-GAP (no internet — Cognito-only via PrivateLink, must delete Cognito domain)"

  CertInstructions:

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito user pool for an application called "researchapp" and "AgentCore", with MFA set to optional using software tokens, email as username and auto-verified, and two user groups (admin and customer) where the admin group has higher precedence. The template should include a web app client using the authorization code flow with callback URLs set to http://localhost:8501/ and https://example.com/auth/callback, and a machine-to-machine client using client credentials flow with a generated secret. Both clients should use a custom resource server with a read scope. Additionally, include a Lambda function (not wired as an active trigger) that would add new users to the customer group. All relevant configuration - such as client IDs, secrets, user pool ID, OAuth scopes, discovery URL, token URL, authorize URL, and the Cognito domain - must be stored in SSM Parameter Store under the path /app/researchapp/agentcore/. The template should accept three parameters with defaults: UserPoolName (TemplateGatewayPool), MachineAppClientName (TemplateMachineClient), and WebAppClientName (TemplateWebClient).
ground_truth_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'CloudFormation template for AgentCore Strands Template with Cognito'
Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: Cognito Configuration
        Parameters:
          - UserPoolName
          - MachineAppClientName
          - WebAppClientName

Parameters:

  UserPoolName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'TemplateGatewayPool'
    Description: 'Name of the Cognito User Pool'

  MachineAppClientName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'TemplateMachineClient'
    Description: 'Name of the Cognito User Pool Application Client'

  WebAppClientName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'TemplateWebClient'
    Description: 'Name of the Cognito User Pool Web Application Client'

Resources:

  UserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: !Ref UserPoolName
      MfaConfiguration: 'OPTIONAL'
      EnabledMfas:
        - SOFTWARE_TOKEN_MFA
      UsernameConfiguration:
        CaseSensitive: false
      UsernameAttributes:
        - email  # <--- Use email as username
      AutoVerifiedAttributes:
        - email  # <--- Auto-verify email if you want to skip confirmation step
      # LambdaConfig:
      #   PostConfirmation: !GetAtt PostSignupFunction.Arn

  AdminGroup:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolGroup
    Properties:
      GroupName: admin
      Description: Administrator group
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Precedence: 1  # Higher priority (lower number = higher precedence)

  CustomerGroup:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolGroup
    Properties:
      GroupName: customer
      Description: Regular customer group
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Precedence: 2

  WebUserPoolClient:
    DependsOn: ResourceServer
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Ref WebAppClientName
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      GenerateSecret: false  # Don't use secret for SPA or web apps
      AllowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      AllowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
        - email
        - profile
        - !Join
            - ''
            - - 'default-m2m-resource-server-'
              - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
              - '/read'
      AllowedOAuthFlowsUserPoolClient: true
      CallbackURLs:
        - http://localhost:8501/
        - https://example.com/auth/callback
      LogoutURLs:
        - http://localhost:8501/
      SupportedIdentityProviders:
        - COGNITO
      AccessTokenValidity: 60
      IdTokenValidity: 60
      RefreshTokenValidity: 30
      TokenValidityUnits:
        AccessToken: minutes
        IdToken: minutes
        RefreshToken: days
      EnableTokenRevocation: true

  MachineUserPoolClient:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    DependsOn: ResourceServer
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Ref MachineAppClientName
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      GenerateSecret: true
      ExplicitAuthFlows:
        - ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH
      RefreshTokenValidity: 1
      AccessTokenValidity: 60
      IdTokenValidity: 60
      TokenValidityUnits:
        AccessToken: minutes
        IdToken: minutes
        RefreshToken: days
      AllowedOAuthFlows:
        - client_credentials
      AllowedOAuthScopes:
        - !Join
          - ''
          - - 'default-m2m-resource-server-'
            - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
            - '/read'
      AllowedOAuthFlowsUserPoolClient: true
      SupportedIdentityProviders:
        - COGNITO
      EnableTokenRevocation: true

  ResourceServer:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolResourceServer
    Properties:
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Identifier: !Join
        - '-'
        - - 'default-m2m-resource-server'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
      Name: !Join
        - '-'
        - - 'Default M2M Resource Server '
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
      Scopes:
        - ScopeName: 'read'
          ScopeDescription: 'An example scope created by Amazon Cognito quick start'

  UserPoolDomain:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolDomain
    Properties:
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Domain: !Join
        - ''
        - - !Ref 'AWS::Region'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]

  PostSignupFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AllowBasicLogs
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: arn:aws:logs:*:*:*
        - PolicyName: Cognito
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cognito-idp:AdminAddUserToGroup
                Resource: "*"

  PostSignupFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Runtime: python3.13
      Role: !GetAtt PostSignupFunctionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 10
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import boto3

          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              user_pool_id = event['userPoolId']
              username = event['userName']
              client = boto3.client('cognito-idp')

              # Add user to 'customer' group
              try:
                  client.admin_add_user_to_group(
                      UserPoolId=user_pool_id,
                      Username=username,
                      GroupName='Customer'
                  )
                  print(f"User {username} added to 'customer' group.")
              except Exception as e:
                  print(f"Error adding user to group: {e}")

              return event

  CognitoMachineClientIdParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/machine_client_id
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref MachineUserPoolClient
      Description: Machine Cognito client ID
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoMachineClientSecretParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_secret
      Type: String
      Value: !GetAtt MachineUserPoolClient.ClientSecret
      Description: Machine Cognito client secret
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoWebClientIdParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/web_client_id
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref WebUserPoolClient
      Description: Cognito client ID for web app
      Tags:
        Application: CustomerSuppor

  UserPoolIdParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/userpool_id
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref UserPool
      Description: Cognito client ID
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoAuthScopeParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_auth_scope
      Type: String
      Value: !Join
        - ''
        - - 'default-m2m-resource-server-'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
          - '/read'
      Description: OAuth2 scope for Cognito auth
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoDiscoveryURLParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_discovery_url
      Type: String
      Value: !Sub 'https://cognito-idp.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${UserPool}/.well-known/openid-configuration'
      Description: OAuth2 Discovery URL
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoTokenURLParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_token_url
      Type: String
      Value: !Join
        - ''
        - - !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
          - !Sub '.auth.${AWS::Region}.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/token'
      Description: OAuth2 Token URL
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoAuthorizeURLParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_auth_url
      Type: String
      Value: !Join
        - ''
        - - !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
          - !Sub '.auth.${AWS::Region}.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/authorize'
      Description: OAuth2 Token URL
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoDomainParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_domain
      Type: String
      Value: !Join
        - ''
        - - !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
          - !Sub '.auth.${AWS::Region}.amazoncognito.com'
      Description: Cognito hosted domain for OAuth2
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained GraphQL API for cryptocurrency ticker data, named CryptoTickerAPI, using AWS AppSync with API key authentication, backed by a DynamoDB table named APIDataTable with a composite primary key (hash key hk and range key sk, both strings) using on-demand billing and server-side encryption disabled, and with a deletion policy of Retain to preserve data; the API should expose a Query.ticker field that, when invoked with a ticker symbol, fetches the current price from the CoinGecko API via an HTTP data source and then stores a historical price record (including ticker, price in USD, and timestamp) into the DynamoDB table using a pipeline resolver composed of two AppSync functions, and also expose a priceHistory field on the TickerInfo type that queries the DynamoDB table for all records matching that ticker, sorted in descending order by the range key, with a default limit of 25 items and support for pagination via a nextToken argument; the template must include the necessary IAM roles and policies for AppSync to assume and interact with both the DynamoDB table and the external HTTP endpoint, and should create a default API key after the schema is defined.
ground_truth_code:
Resources:
  APIDataTableD1E8D052:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: hk
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: sk
          KeyType: RANGE
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: hk
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: sk
          AttributeType: S
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: false
      TableName: APIDataTable
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: InfraStack/APIDataTable/Resource
  APIAccessRoleB69CDA23:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: appsync.amazonaws.com
        Version: "2012-10-17"
      Policies:
        - PolicyDocument:
            Statement:
              - Action: dynamodb:*
                Effect: Allow
                Resource:
                  Fn::GetAtt:
                    - APIDataTableD1E8D052
                    - Arn
                Sid: APIAccessDynamoDB
            Version: "2012-10-17"
          PolicyName: DDBAccess
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: InfraStack/APIAccessRole/Resource
  APIAccessRoleDefaultPolicy55859C45:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Action:
              - dynamodb:BatchGetItem
              - dynamodb:GetRecords
              - dynamodb:GetShardIterator
              - dynamodb:Query
              - dynamodb:GetItem
              - dynamodb:Scan
              - dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem
              - dynamodb:BatchWriteItem
              - dynamodb:PutItem
              - dynamodb:UpdateItem
              - dynamodb:DeleteItem
            Effect: Allow
            Resource:
              - Fn::GetAtt:
                  - APIDataTableD1E8D052
                  - Arn
              - Ref: AWS::NoValue
        Version: "2012-10-17"
      PolicyName: APIAccessRoleDefaultPolicy55859C45
      Roles:
        - Ref: APIAccessRoleB69CDA23
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: InfraStack/APIAccessRole/DefaultPolicy/Resource
  AppSyncAPID0E760D2:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLApi
    Properties:
      AuthenticationType: API_KEY
      Name: CryptoTickerAPI
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: InfraStack/AppSyncAPI/Resource
  AppSyncAPISchemaB1D44998:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLSchema
    Properties:
      ApiId:
        Fn::GetAtt:
          - AppSyncAPID0E760D2
          - ApiId
      Definition: |-
        type Query {
            # Our ticker resolver fetches data from coingecko's API and then inserts a historical price data object
            # into our DynamoDB table using an AppSync pipeline resolver.
            ticker(ticker: String!): TickerInfo
        }

        # Contains information about the ticker present in the URL.
        type TickerInfo {
            # The ticker & latestPrice are returned as part of the object returned by the Query.ticker resolver
            ticker: String!
            latestPrice: PriceData

            # The priceHistory field has an attached unit resolver that reads the price history directly out of DynamoDB.
            # You may pass the limit and nextToken arguments to paginate through the price data.
            priceHistory(limit: Int, nextToken: String): HistoricalPriceConnection
        }

        # The purpose of the `XConnection` pattern is to provide pagination to resources with potentially
        # large numbers of items such as this price history. The limit & nextToken arguments on `TickerInfo.priceHistory`
        # are used to control the results in this connection.
        type HistoricalPriceConnection {
            nextToken: String
            items: [HistoricalPriceData]
        }
        type HistoricalPriceData {
            ticker: String
            priceUSD: Float
            timestamp: String
        }
        type PriceData {
            usd: Float
        }
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: InfraStack/AppSyncAPI/Schema
  AppSyncAPIDefaultApiKey016AAF21:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::ApiKey
    Properties:
      ApiId:
        Fn::GetAtt:
          - AppSyncAPID0E760D2
          - ApiId
    DependsOn:
      - AppSyncAPISchemaB1D44998
    Metadata:
      aws:cdk:path: InfraStack/AppSyncAPI/DefaultApiKey
  DDBTableDataSource43262F9B:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::DataSource
    Properties:

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a MediaPackage channel for live streaming with HLS and DASH origin endpoints, where the origin endpoints’ origination is set to DENY if a user-provided ArchiveBucket parameter is supplied (to support live-to-VOD workflows), and the DASH endpoint always uses a hardcoded segment duration of 2 seconds while the HLS endpoint uses a user-specified segment duration parameter; the template optionally provisions VOD workflows using a user-provided VodSourceBucket for source content and the ArchiveBucket for live-to-VOD storage, with the IAM role necessary for MediaPackage to access those buckets, and supports specifying the output type (defaulting to APPLE_HLS, with ISO_DASH and ALL also supported), manifest name, segment duration in seconds for HLS, startover window in seconds, a logical name prefix for resource naming, and tagging with environment and custom key-value tags.
ground_truth_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: 2010-09-09
Description: aws-cloudformation-templates/media/mediapackage sets Elemental MediaPackage.

Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: 'MediaPackage Configuration'
        Parameters:
          - ArchiveBucket
          - ManifestName
          - OutputType
          - StartoverWindowSeconds
          - SegmentDurationSeconds
          - VodSourceBucket
      - Label:
          default: 'Tag Configuration'
        Parameters:
          - LogicalName
          - Environment
          - TagKey
          - TagValue

Parameters:
  ArchiveBucket:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: The S3 bucket Name LIVE-to-VOD contents are stored.
  ManifestName:
    Type: String
    Default: index
    Description: A short string that's appended to the end of the endpoint URL to create a unique path to this endpoint [required]
  OutputType:
    Type: String
    AllowedValues:
      - APPLE_HLS
      - ISO_DASH
      - ALL
    Default: APPLE_HLS
    Description: Output type [required]
  StartoverWindowSeconds:
    Type: Number
    Default: 0
    Description: Maximum duration seconds of content to retain for startover playback [required]
    MinValue: 0
  SegmentDurationSeconds:
    Type: String
    Default: 3
    Description: Duration (in seconds) of each fragment [required]
  VodSourceBucket:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: The S3 bucket Name VOD contents exist.
  LogicalName:
    Type: String
    Default: MediaPackage
    AllowedPattern: .+
    Description: The custom prefix name [required]
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    AllowedValues:
      - production
      - test
      - development
  TagKey:
    Type: String
    Default: createdby
    AllowedPattern: .+
  TagValue:
    Type: String
    Default: aws-cloudformation-templates
    AllowedPattern: .+

Conditions:
  CreateVODWorkflow: !Not [ !Equals [ !Ref VodSourceBucket, '' ] ]
  CreateLiveToVODWorkflow: !Not [ !Equals [ !Ref ArchiveBucket, '' ] ]
  CreateHlsEndPoint: !Or [ !Equals [ !Ref OutputType, APPLE_HLS ], !Equals [ !Ref OutputType, ALL ] ]
  CreateDashEndPoint: !Or [ !Equals [ !Ref OutputType, ISO_DASH ], !Equals [ !Ref OutputType, ALL ] ]
  CreateHlsVODWorkflow: !And [ !Not [ !Equals [ !Ref VodSourceBucket, '' ] ], !Or [ !Equals [ !Ref OutputType, APPLE_HLS ], !Equals [ !Ref OutputType, ALL ] ] ]
  CreateDashVODWorkflow: !And [ !Not [ !Equals [ !Ref VodSourceBucket, '' ] ], !Or [ !Equals [ !Ref OutputType, ISO_DASH ], !Equals [ !Ref OutputType, ALL ] ] ]

Resources:
  # IAM Role
  IAMRoleForMediaPackage:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: mediapackage.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Description: A role required for MediaPackage to access S3.
      Policies:
        # Allow MediaPackage to access S3 for VOD workflows.
        - !If
          - CreateVODWorkflow
          - PolicyName: S3Read
            PolicyDocument:
              Version: 2012-10-17
              Statement:
                - Effect: Allow
                  Action:
                    - s3:GetObject
                    - s3:GetBucketLocation
                    - s3:GetBucketRequestPayment
                    - s3:ListBucket
                  Resource:
                    - !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:::${VodSourceBucket}/*'
                    - !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:::${VodSourceBucket}'
          - !Ref AWS::NoValue
        # Allow MediaPackage to access S3 for Live-to-VOD workflows.
        - !If
          - CreateLiveToVODWorkflow
          - PolicyName: S3Write
            PolicyDocument:
              Version: 2012-10-17
              Statement:
                - Effect: Allow
                  Action:
                    - s3:PutObject
                    - s3:ListBucket
                    - s3:GetBucketLocation
                  Resource:
                    - !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:::${ArchiveBucket}/*'
                    - !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:::${ArchiveBucket}'
          - !Ref AWS::NoValue
        # Allow MediaPackage to access SecretsManager.
        - PolicyName: SecretsManager
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: 2012-10-17
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecrets
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecretVersionIds
                Resource:
                  - '*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iam:GetRole
                  - iam:PassRole
                Resource:
                  - '*'
      RoleName: !Sub ${LogicalName}-MediaPackage-${AWS::Region}
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
  # MediaPackage
  MediaPackageChannel:
    Type: AWS::MediaPackage::Channel
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub Media Package Channel for ${LogicalName}
      Id: !Ref LogicalName
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
  MediaPackageHlsOriginEndpoint:
    Condition: CreateHlsEndPoint
    Type: AWS::MediaPackage::OriginEndpoint
    Properties:
      ChannelId: !Ref MediaPackageChannel
      Description: !Sub Media Package OriginEndpoint for ${LogicalName}
      HlsPackage:
        AdMarkers: NONE
        IncludeIframeOnlyStream: false
        SegmentDurationSeconds: !Ref SegmentDurationSeconds
      Id: !Sub ${LogicalName}-Hls
      ManifestName: !Ref ManifestName
      Origination: !If
        - CreateLiveToVODWorkflow
        - DENY
        - ALLOW
      StartoverWindowSeconds: !Ref StartoverWindowSeconds
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
      TimeDelaySeconds: 0
  MediaPackageDashOriginEndpoint:
    Condition: CreateDashEndPoint
    Type: AWS::MediaPackage::OriginEndpoint
    Properties:
      ChannelId: !Ref MediaPackageChannel
      DashPackage:
        ManifestLayout: FULL
        ManifestWindowSeconds: 60
        MinBufferTimeSeconds: 10
        MinUpdatePeriodSeconds: 2
        Profile: NONE
        SegmentDurationSeconds: 2
        SegmentTemplateFormat: NUMBER_WITH_TIMELINE
        SuggestedPresentationDelaySeconds: 20
      Description: !Sub Media Package OriginEndpoint for ${LogicalName}
      Id: !Sub ${LogicalName}-Dash
      ManifestName: !Ref ManifestName
      Origination: !If
        - CreateLiveToVODWorkflow
        - DENY
        - ALLOW
      StartoverWindowSeconds: !Ref StartoverWindowSeconds
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
      TimeDelaySeconds: 0
  MediaPackageHlsAsset:
    Condition: CreateHlsVODWorkflow
    Type: AWS::MediaPackage::Asset
    Properties:
      Id: !Sub ${LogicalName}-Hls
      PackagingGroupId: !Ref MediaPackagePackagingGroup
      SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:::${VodSourceBucket}'
      SourceRoleArn: !GetAtt IAMRoleForMediaPackage.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
  MediaPackageDashAsset:
    Condition: CreateDashVODWorkflow
    Type: AWS::MediaPackage::Asset
    Properties:
      Id: !Sub ${LogicalName}-Dash
      PackagingGroupId: !Ref MediaPackagePackagingGroup
      SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:::${VodSourceBucket}'
      SourceRoleArn: !GetAtt IAMRoleForMediaPackage.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
  MediaPackagePackagingGroup:
    Condition: CreateVODWorkflow
    Type: AWS::MediaPackage::PackagingGroup
    Properties:
      Id: !Ref LogicalName
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
  MediaPackageHlsPackagingConfiguration:
    Condition: CreateHlsVODWorkflow
    Type: AWS::MediaPackage::PackagingConfiguration
    Properties:
      HlsPackage:
        HlsManifests:
          - IncludeIframeOnlyStream: false
            ManifestName: !Ref ManifestName
            RepeatExtXKey: false
        SegmentDurationSeconds: !Ref SegmentDurationSeconds
        UseAudioRenditionGroup: false
      Id: !Sub ${LogicalName}-Hls
      PackagingGroupId: !Ref MediaPackagePackagingGroup
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue
  MediaPackageDashPackagingConfiguration:
    Condition: CreateDashVODWorkflow
    Type: AWS::MediaPackage::PackagingConfiguration
    Properties:
      DashPackage:
        DashManifests:
          - ManifestLayout: FULL
            ManifestName: !Ref ManifestName
            MinBufferTimeSeconds: 30
            Profile: NONE
        SegmentDurationSeconds: !Ref SegmentDurationSeconds
        SegmentTemplateFormat: NUMBER_WITH_TIMELINE
      Id: !Sub ${LogicalName}-Dash
      PackagingGroupId: !Ref MediaPackagePackagingGroup
      Tags:
        - Key: environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: !Ref TagKey
          Value: !Ref TagValue

Outputs:
  ChannelId:
    Description: Channel Id
    Value: !Ref MediaPackageChannel
  HlsEndpointUrl:
    Description: Endpoint Url
    Value: !If
      - CreateHlsEndPoint
      - !GetAtt MediaPackageHlsOriginEndpoint.Url
      - ''
  ManifestFile:
    Description: A short string that's appended to the end of the endpoint URL to create a unique path to this endpoint
    Value: !Ref ManifestName
  DashEndpointUrl:
    Description: Endpoint Url
    Value: !If
      - CreateDashEndPoint
      - !GetAtt MediaPackageDashOriginEndpoint.Url
      - ''

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained ECS Fargate service that is reachable through a public Application Load Balancer while the service's own tasks run in private subnets. The stack should build its own VPC with two public subnets and two private subnets across separate availability zones, an internet gateway, and a single NAT gateway so the private subnets can reach the internet. Provision an ECS cluster, an internet-facing Application Load Balancer listening on port 80 with a default fixed 404 response, and a listener rule that forwards requests matching a configurable URL path pattern and priority to a target group backed by the Fargate service. Accept parameters for the environment name, service name, container image (defaulting to nginx), container port, CPU, memory, desired task count, and an optional custom IAM role for the task containers, and create the ECS task execution role and a CloudWatch log group for the container's logs. The load balancer should only allow inbound HTTP traffic on port 80 from the internet, and the service's own security group should only accept traffic from the load balancer.
ground_truth_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Deploy a service on AWS Fargate, hosted in a private subnet, but accessible via a public load balancer.
Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: The name of the environment to add this service to
  ServiceName:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: A name for the service
  ImageUrl:
    Type: String
    Default: nginx
    Description: The url of a docker image that contains the application process that
                 will handle the traffic for this service
  ContainerPort:
    Type: Number
    Default: 80
    Description: What port number the application inside the docker container is binding to
  ContainerCpu:
    Type: Number
    Default: 256
    Description: How much CPU to give the container. 1024 is 1 CPU
  ContainerMemory:
    Type: Number
    Default: 512
    Description: How much memory in megabytes to give the container
  Path:
    Type: String
    Default: "*"
    Description: A path on the load balancer that this service
                 should be connected to. Use * to send all load balancer
                 traffic to this service.
  Priority:
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
    Description: The priority for the routing rule added to the load balancer.
                 This only applies if your have multiple services which have been
                 assigned to different paths on the load balancer.
  DesiredCount:
    Type: Number
    Default: 2
    Description: How many copies of the service task to run
  Role:
    Type: String
    Default: ""
    Description: (Optional) An IAM role to give the service's containers if the code within needs to
                 access other AWS resources like S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, etc

Conditions:
  HasCustomRole: !Not [ !Equals [!Ref 'Role', ''] ]

Resources:
  # This template used to be one microservice out of a multi-stack
  # reference architecture (network/cluster/ALB stacks all imported by
  # EnvironmentName-prefixed exports it never created itself). Made
  # self-contained by building a minimal VPC + ECS Cluster + ALB stack
  # inline instead: 2 public subnets (ALB + NAT) / 2 private subnets
  # (Fargate tasks), a single NAT Gateway, an internet-facing ALB with a
  # default 404 listener (each service's own ListenerRule adds real
  # routing on top, matching the aws-samples/ecs-refarch-cloudformation
  # pattern this file is itself based on).
  Vpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
  VpcGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetOne:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PublicSubnetTwo:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.1.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetOneRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.2.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
  PrivateSubnetTwoRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      CidrBlock: 10.0.3.0/24
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
  PublicSubnetOneRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetOne
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  PublicSubnetTwoRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetTwo
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
  NatEip:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
  NatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatEip.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetOne
  PrivateRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
  PrivateRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway
  PrivateSubnetOneRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable
  PrivateSubnetTwoRouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable

  Cluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Ref EnvironmentName

  ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy

  ContainerSecurityGroupRes:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-containers'
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 0
          ToPort: 65535
          SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref PublicLoadBalancerSecurityGroup

  PublicLoadBalancerSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-alb'
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

  # internet-facing (AVD-AWS-0053) and plain HTTP (AVD-AWS-0054) are the
  # scenario's own stated intent ("accessible via a public load balancer")
  # -- no real domain is available for a validated ACM cert, so this stays
  # HTTP-only rather than fabricating HTTPS. Both suppressed deliberately.
  #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0053
  PublicLoadBalancer:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties:
      Scheme: internet-facing
      Subnets:
        - !Ref PublicSubnetOne
        - !Ref PublicSubnetTwo
      SecurityGroups:
        - !Ref PublicLoadBalancerSecurityGroup
      LoadBalancerAttributes:
        - Key: routing.http.drop_invalid_header_fields.enabled
          Value: 'true'

  #trivy:ignore:AVD-AWS-0054
  PublicListenerRes:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener
    Properties:
      LoadBalancerArn: !Ref PublicLoadBalancer
      Port: 80
      Protocol: HTTP
      DefaultActions:
        - Type: fixed-response
          FixedResponseConfig:
            StatusCode: '404'

  #Um grupo de logs para armazenar os logs stdout dos contêineres deste serviço
  LogGrupo:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}

  # A definição da tarefa. Esta é uma descrição simples de metadados do que
  # contêiner a ser executado e quais requisitos de recursos ele possui.
  TaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
      Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt ECSTaskExecutionRoleRes.Arn
      TaskRoleArn:
        Fn::If:
          - 'HasCustomRole'
          - !Ref 'Role'
          - !Ref "AWS::NoValue"
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          Cpu: !Ref 'ContainerCpu'
          Memory: !Ref 'ContainerMemory'
          Image: !Ref 'ImageUrl'
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: 'awslogs'
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Sub ${EnvironmentName}-service-${ServiceName}
              awslogs-region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
              awslogs-stream-prefix: !Ref 'ServiceName'

  # O serviço. O serviço é um recurso que permite executar vários
  # cópias de um tipo de tarefa e reúna seus logs e métricas também
  # como monitorar o número de tarefas em execução e substituir qualquer uma que tenha travado
  Service:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    DependsOn: LoadBalancerRule
    Properties:
      ServiceName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Cluster: !Ref Cluster
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      DeploymentConfiguration:
        MaximumPercent: 200
        MinimumHealthyPercent: 75
      DesiredCount: !Ref 'DesiredCount'
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          AssignPublicIp: DISABLED
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref ContainerSecurityGroupRes
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetOneRes
            - !Ref PrivateSubnetTwoRes
      TaskDefinition: !Ref 'TaskDefinition'
      LoadBalancers:
        - ContainerName: !Ref 'ServiceName'
          ContainerPort: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
          TargetGroupArn: !Ref 'TargetGroup'

  #Um grupo-alvo. Isto é usado para manter o controle de todas as tarefas, e
  # quais endereços IP/números de porta eles têm. Você mesmo pode consultar,
  # para usar os endereços você mesmo, mas na maioria das vezes esse grupo-alvo é apenas
  # conectado a um balanceador de carga de aplicativo ou balanceador de carga de rede, então
  # pode distribuir automaticamente o tráfego entre todos os alvos.
  TargetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
    Properties:
      HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 6
      HealthCheckPath: /
      HealthCheckProtocol: HTTP
      HealthCheckTimeoutSeconds: 5
      HealthyThresholdCount: 2
      TargetType: ip
      Name: !Ref 'ServiceName'
      Port: !Ref 'ContainerPort'
      Protocol: HTTP
      UnhealthyThresholdCount: 2
      VpcId: !Ref Vpc

  #Crie uma regra no balanceador de carga para rotear o tráfego para o grupo de destino
  LoadBalancerRule:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::ListenerRule
    Properties:
      Actions:
        - TargetGroupArn: !Ref 'TargetGroup'
          Type: 'forward'
      Conditions:
        - Field: path-pattern
          Values: [!Ref 'Path']
      ListenerArn: !Ref PublicListenerRes
      Priority: !Ref 'Priority'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'cfn-modules: AWS DynamoDB table'

    Type: String
    Default: ''
  KmsKeyModule:
    Description: 'Optional but recommended stack name of kms-key module.'

  TableName:

    Description: 'Name of the partition key.'
    Type: String
    Default: id
  PartitionKeyType:
    Description: 'Type of the partition key.'
    Type: String
    Default: S
    AllowedValues: [S, N, B]
  SortKeyName:
    Description: 'Optional name of the sort key.'
    Type: String
    Default: ''
  SortKeyType:
    Description: 'Type of the sort key (if SortKeyName is set).'
    Type: String
    Default: N
    AllowedValues: [S, N, B]
  BillingAndScalingMode:
    Description: 'Specify how you are charged for read and write throughput and how you manage capacity.'
    Type: String
    Default: PROVISIONED
    AllowedValues: [PROVISIONED, ONDEMAND]
  MaxWriteCapacityUnits:
    Description: 'Maximum write capacity units used during auto scaling (ignored when BillingAndScalingMode := ONDEMAND).'
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
  MinWriteCapacityUnits:
    Description: 'Minimum write capacity units used during auto scaling (ignored when BillingAndScalingMode := ONDEMAND).'
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
  WriteCapacityUnitsUtilizationTarget:
    Description: 'Target write capacity utilization (in percent) that auto scaling tries to achieve (if you have spiky writes, a lower number is better; ignored when BillingAndScalingMode := ONDEMAND).'
    Type: Number
    Default: 80
  MaxReadCapacityUnits:
    Description: 'Maximum read capacity units used during auto scaling (ignored when BillingAndScalingMode := ONDEMAND).'
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
  MinReadCapacityUnits:
    Description: 'Minimum read capacity units used during auto scaling (ignored when BillingAndScalingMode := ONDEMAND).'
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
  ReadCapacityUnitsUtilizationTarget:
    Description: 'Target read capacity utilization (in percent) that auto scaling tries to achieve (if you have spiky reads, a lower number is better; ignored when BillingAndScalingMode := ONDEMAND).'
    Type: Number
    Default: 80
  Encryption:
    Description: 'Deprecated in v1, will be removed in v3, use KmsKeyModule instead! Enable server side encryption using KMS (AWS managed) CMK.'
    Type: String
    Default: false
    AllowedValues: [aws, false]
  StreamViewType:
    Description: 'Determines the information that the stream captures when an item in the table is modified.'
    Type: String
    Default: DISABLED

  TtlAttributeName:

    Type: String
    Default: ''

Conditions:

    Properties:

      - - AttributeName: !Ref PartitionKeyName

        - AttributeName: !Ref SortKeyName

      - - AttributeName: !Ref PartitionKeyName
