prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC, with a parameterized identifier and CIDR block, that has both an IPv4 range and an Amazon-provided IPv6 range associated with it, spread across three Availability Zones. Include a parameter that lets the deployer choose whether to include public subnets at all; when enabled, the stack should create three public subnets, one per Availability Zone, each carved out of the VPC's own IPv4 and IPv6 ranges, an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC, and a single public route table with a default route to the internet, associated with all three public subnets. Regardless of that choice, the stack should always create three private subnets, again one per Availability Zone with both IPv4 and IPv6 ranges, and a single private route table associated with all of them, though it does not need a default route to the internet. Expose the VPC ID and the lists of public and private subnet IDs as stack outputs.

We need a CloudFormation template that provisions the full set of IAM identities and permissions required to bootstrap and operate the Cluster API Provider for AWS, so that a Kubernetes cluster's control plane, controller manager, and worker nodes can each assume a dedicated role with least-privilege access. Create separate IAM roles for the control plane, the controllers, the worker nodes, and a role dedicated to the EKS control plane, each with a matching instance profile where relevant, assumable by the EC2 service (and, for the controllers role, also by EKS Pods), and each carrying the AWS managed policies appropriate to its function, such as the managed EKS cluster, worker node, and CNI policies. Attach managed IAM policies to the control plane and worker node roles granting the EC2, Elastic Load Balancing, Auto Scaling, ECR, Secrets Manager, and Systems Manager permissions the AWS cloud provider integration needs to manage those resources on the cluster's behalf, and attach a broader managed policy to the controllers and control plane roles covering the EC2 networking, load balancing, auto scaling, EKS cluster and nodegroup management, and related service-linked role creation permissions the cluster API controllers require. Also create an IAM group and an IAM user representing a bootstrapper identity used to run cluster lifecycle operations, with the group granted the same controller-level managed policy.

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'VPC Infrastructure for OpenSearch Cross-Region Resilience - Can be deployed in both regions'

Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: Environment name prefix for resources

  VpcCIDR:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.0.0/16
    Description: CIDR block for VPC
    AllowedPattern: '^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])(\/([0-9]|[1-2][0-9]|3[0-2]))$'

  PrivateSubnet1CIDR:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.1.0/24
    Description: CIDR block for private subnet 1
    AllowedPattern: '^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])(\/([0-9]|[1-2][0-9]|3[0-2]))$'

  PrivateSubnet2CIDR:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.2.0/24
    Description: CIDR block for private subnet 2
    AllowedPattern: '^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])(\/([0-9]|[1-2][0-9]|3[0-2]))$'

  PrivateSubnet3CIDR:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.3.0/24
    Description: CIDR block for private subnet 3
    AllowedPattern: '^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])(\/([0-9]|[1-2][0-9]|3[0-2]))$'

  PublicSubnet1CIDR:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.101.0/24
    Description: CIDR block for public subnet 1 (for NAT Gateway)
    AllowedPattern: '^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])(\/([0-9]|[1-2][0-9]|3[0-2]))$'

  PublicSubnet2CIDR:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.102.0/24
    Description: CIDR block for public subnet 2 (for NAT Gateway)
    AllowedPattern: '^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])(\/([0-9]|[1-2][0-9]|3[0-2]))$'

  PublicSubnet3CIDR:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.103.0/24
    Description: CIDR block for public subnet 3 (for NAT Gateway)
    AllowedPattern: '^(([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])\.){3}([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|2[0-4][0-9]|25[0-5])(\/([0-9]|[1-2][0-9]|3[0-2]))$'

  EnableNATGateway:
    Type: String
    Default: 'true'
    AllowedValues:
      - 'true'
      - 'false'
    Description: Enable NAT Gateway for private subnet internet access (recommended for production)

  NATGatewayRedundancy:
    Type: String
    Default: 'single'
    AllowedValues:
      - 'single'
      - 'high-availability'
    Description: Single NAT Gateway (cost-effective) or one per AZ (high availability)

Conditions:
  CreateNATGateway: !Equals [!Ref EnableNATGateway, 'true']
  CreateHighAvailabilityNAT: !And
    - !Condition CreateNATGateway
    - !Equals [!Ref NATGatewayRedundancy, 'high-availability']
  CreateSingleNAT: !And
    - !Condition CreateNATGateway
    - !Equals [!Ref NATGatewayRedundancy, 'single']

Resources:
  # VPC
  VPC:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: !Ref VpcCIDR
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-vpc'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  # Internet Gateway
  InternetGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-igw'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  InternetGatewayAttachment:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
      VpcId: !Ref VPC

  # Public Subnets
  # Note: Public subnets host NAT Gateways only. NAT Gateways use Elastic IPs, not auto-assigned public IPs.
  # MapPublicIpOnLaunch is set to false as it's not required for NAT Gateway functionality.
  # MSK and other workloads run in private subnets.
  PublicSubnet1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      CidrBlock: !Ref PublicSubnet1CIDR
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-public-subnet-1'
        - Key: Type
          Value: Public

  PublicSubnet2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
      CidrBlock: !Ref PublicSubnet2CIDR
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-public-subnet-2'
        - Key: Type
          Value: Public

  PublicSubnet3:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [2, !GetAZs '']
      CidrBlock: !Ref PublicSubnet3CIDR
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-public-subnet-3'
        - Key: Type
          Value: Public

  # Private Subnets
  PrivateSubnet1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      CidrBlock: !Ref PrivateSubnet1CIDR
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-private-subnet-1'
        - Key: Type
          Value: Private

  PrivateSubnet2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
      CidrBlock: !Ref PrivateSubnet2CIDR
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-private-subnet-2'
        - Key: Type
          Value: Private

  PrivateSubnet3:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [2, !GetAZs '']
      CidrBlock: !Ref PrivateSubnet3CIDR
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-private-subnet-3'
        - Key: Type
          Value: Private

  # NAT Gateways
  NatGateway1EIP:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    DependsOn: InternetGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-nat-eip-1'

  NatGateway2EIP:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    Condition: CreateHighAvailabilityNAT
    DependsOn: InternetGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-nat-eip-2'

  NatGateway3EIP:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    Condition: CreateHighAvailabilityNAT
    DependsOn: InternetGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-nat-eip-3'

  NatGateway1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatGateway1EIP.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet1
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-nat-1'

  NatGateway2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Condition: CreateHighAvailabilityNAT
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatGateway2EIP.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet2
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-nat-2'

  NatGateway3:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Condition: CreateHighAvailabilityNAT
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatGateway3EIP.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet3
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-nat-3'

  # Public Route Table
  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-public-routes'

  DefaultPublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    DependsOn: InternetGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway

  PublicSubnet1RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet1

  PublicSubnet2RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet2

  PublicSubnet3RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnet3

  # Private Route Tables
  PrivateRouteTable1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-private-routes-1'

  DefaultPrivateRoute1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Condition: CreateNATGateway
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable1
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway1

  PrivateSubnet1RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable1
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnet1

  # Route Table 2 - Uses NAT Gateway 2 if HA, otherwise NAT Gateway 1
  PrivateRouteTable2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-private-routes-2'

  DefaultPrivateRoute2HA:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Condition: CreateHighAvailabilityNAT
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable2
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway2

  DefaultPrivateRoute2Single:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Condition: CreateSingleNAT
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable2
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway1

  PrivateSubnet2RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable2
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnet2

  # Route Table 3 - Uses NAT Gateway 3 if HA, otherwise NAT Gateway 1
  PrivateRouteTable3:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${EnvironmentName}-private-routes-3'

  DefaultPrivateRoute3HA:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Condition: CreateHighAvailabilityNAT
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable3
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway3

  DefaultPrivateRoute3Single:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Condition: CreateSingleNAT
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable3
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      NatGatewayId: !Ref NatGateway1

  PrivateSubnet3RouteTableAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PrivateRouteTable3
      SubnetId: !Ref PrivateSubnet3

  # VPC Flow Logs (Optional but recommended)
  # Note: RoleName is omitted to allow CloudFormation stack updates that require resource replacement
  VPCFlowLogsRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'

          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: CloudWatchLogPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogStream'
                  - 'logs:PutLogEvents'
                  - 'logs:DescribeLogStreams'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/vpc/${EnvironmentName}:*'
              - Effect: Allow

                  - 'logs:DescribeLogGroups'

  VPCFlowLogsLogGroup:

Description: 'Private VPC with 4 isolated subnets and VPC endpoints for AWS services (no internet gateway). Includes endpoints for Bedrock, ECR, CloudWatch, DynamoDB, Aurora, and Secrets Manager to enable secure communication without public internet access.'

Metadata:
  'AWS::CloudFormation::Interface':
    ParameterGroups:
    - Label:
        default: 'Environment Configuration'
      Parameters:
      - Environment
    - Label:
        default: 'VPC Configuration'
      Parameters:
      - VpcCidr
      - PrivateSubnet1Cidr
      - PrivateSubnet2Cidr
      - PrivateSubnet3Cidr

Mappings:
  DynamoDBPrefixListIds:
    us-east-1:
      PrefixListId: pl-02cd2c6b
    us-east-2:
      PrefixListId: pl-4ca54025
    us-west-1:
      PrefixListId: pl-6ea54007
    us-west-2:
      PrefixListId: pl-00a54069

Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: 'dev'
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - test
      - prod
    Description: 'Environment name for resource naming'

  VpcCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.0.0.0/16'
    Description: 'CIDR block for the VPC'

  PrivateSubnet3Cidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.0.1.0/24'
    Description: 'CIDR block for the third private subnet'

  PrivateSubnet1Cidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.0.3.0/24'
    Description: 'CIDR block for the first private subnet'

  PrivateSubnet2Cidr:
    Type: String
    Default: '10.0.4.0/24'
    Description: 'CIDR block for the second private subnet'

Resources:
  # VPC
  VPC:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: !Ref VpcCidr
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub 'csvpc-${Environment}-VPC'

  # Private Subnets (no internet access)
  PrivateSubnet1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      CidrBlock: !Ref PrivateSubnet1Cidr
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub 'csvpc-${Environment}-Private-Subnet-1'

  PrivateSubnet2:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a VPC, with a parameterized CIDR block and a name used to tag resources, intended to host an Amazon EKS cluster, spread across three Availability Zones. It should include three public subnets and three private subnets, each with its own CIDR parameter, an Internet Gateway attached to the VPC with a public route table routing to it, and a NAT Gateway with its own Elastic IP in each public subnet, providing outbound internet access for the corresponding private subnet through per-Availability-Zone private route tables. Tag the private subnets appropriately for internal load balancer discovery. The stack should also create a security group intended for the EKS control plane to communicate with worker nodes, and a second security group exposing several application ports, including HTTP, HTTPS, and a handful of custom TCP ports used by an ingress or service mesh gateway, to the internet. Expose the VPC ID, the security group IDs, and the list of all subnet IDs as stack outputs.

---
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: VPC and network configuration for an EKS cluster.

Parameters:
  Name:
    Type: String
    Default: kameshs-gloo-demos
    Description: AWS EKS Cluster Name, the cluster name will be used as VPC/Subnet suffix.

  VpcCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: 172.25.0.0/16
    Description: The CIDR to use for the VPC

  PrivateSubneta:
    Type: String
    Default: 172.25.1.0/24
    Description: The CIDR to use for private subnet in region Zone A

  PrivateSubnetb:
    Type: String
    Default: 172.25.2.0/24
    Description: The CIDR to use for private subnet in region Zone B

  PrivateSubnetc:
    Type: String
    Default: 172.25.3.0/24
    Description: The CIDR to use for private subnet in region Zone C

  PublicSubneta:
    Type: String
    Default: 172.25.5.0/24
    Description: The CIDR to use for public subnet in region Zone A

  PublicSubnetb:
    Type: String
    Default: 172.25.6.0/24
    Description: The CIDR to use for public subnet in region Zone B

  PublicSubnetc:
    Type: String
    Default: 172.25.7.0/24
    Description: The CIDR to use for public subnet in region Zone C

Resources:
  VPC:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: !Ref VpcCidr
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub "${Name}-vpc"

  InternetGateway:
    Type: "AWS::EC2::InternetGateway"
    Properties:
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub "${Name}-igw"

  VPCGatewayAttachment:
    Type: "AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment"
    Properties:
      InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
      VpcId: !Ref VPC

  PublicRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub "${Name}-public-rt"
        - Key: Network
          Value: Public

  PublicRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
      DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
      GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
    DependsOn:
      - VPCGatewayAttachment

  PrivateRouteTableAZ1:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VPC
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub "${Name}-private-rt-zone1"
        - Key: Network

prefix, an EKS cluster name, a VPC ID, a list of security group IDs, a list of private subnet IDs, an S3 bucket name for lifecycle scripts, and optional parameters for a RIG input S3 bucket, a RIG output S3 bucket, a flag to create RIG resources, and a flag to enable gated access, and the role must be named by appending "ExecRole" to the prefix, allow the SageMaker service principal to assume it, be attached to the AWS managed policy for SageMaker cluster instance roles, and include a custom inline policy that grants the EKS CNI plugin permissions for attaching network interfaces, describing instances, tags, network interfaces, instance types, and subnets, and creating tags on network interfaces, along with a second inline policy that grants broader ENI management actions such as assigning private IP addresses, creating, deleting, and modifying network interfaces and permissions, and detaching network interfaces, scoped to instances, network interfaces, and the specified VPC, plus read permissions for VPCs, DHCP options, and security groups, ECR actions for pulling container images, CloudWatch alarm describe permissions, the eks-auth:AssumeRoleForPodIdentity action scoped to the provided EKS cluster, and list and get object access to the lifecycle scripts S3 bucket, and the template must also conditionally create a RIG policy when the RIG flag is true and a RIG input bucket is provided, granting list and get object access to that bucket, allowing Lambda invocation for functions with names containing SageMaker or sagemaker, and when the gated access flag is true, additionally granting get object access to specific S3 access points and buckets and SQS message actions on queues containing SageMaker or sagemaker, and if a separate RIG output bucket is provided, granting full read, write, and delete object access to that bucket, and the template must also conditionally create additional policies for each provided private subnet and security group that grant the same ENI management actions scoped to those specific subnet and security group resources, and all resources must be tagged with a key indicating they are SageMaker HyperPod prerequisites with a value equal to the role name, and the stack should expose the role name and ARN as outputs.

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: 2010-09-09
Description: >-
  This template creates a custom SMTP resource that stores the SMTP
  credentials in Parameter Store under the names "smtp-username" and
  "smtp-password".

Parameters:
  IamAccessKeyVersion:
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
    Description: Version number of the AWS access keys. Increment this number to rotate the keys.
    MinValue: 1
  KmsKeyArn:
    Type: String
    Description: (Optional) ARN of the KMS key used to encrypt the SMTP credentials in Parameter Store
    Default: ""
    AllowedPattern: '^(arn:aws:kms:(us|af|ap|ca|eu|il|mx|me|sa)-(east|west|south|north|southeast|northeast|central)-[1-7]:\d{12}:key\/[a-z0-9]{8}(-[a-z0-9]{4}){3}-[a-z0-9]{12}$)?'
    ConstraintDescription: This value must be a valid ACM certificate ARN format, or left blank
  Username:
    Type: String
    Description: Desired name of the IAM user
    Default: SMTPUser
  LambdaLogRetentionTime:
    Type: Number
    Description: The length of time in days to retain the Sectigo Lambda function execution logs
    Default: 14
    AllowedValues:
      - 1
      - 3
      - 5
      - 7
      - 14
      - 30
      - 60
      - 90
      - 120
      - 150
      - 180
      - 365

Conditions:
  UseCustomKMSKey: !Not [!Equals [!Ref KmsKeyArn, ""]]

Resources:
  SmtpUserGroup:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Group
    Properties:
      GroupName: !Sub ${Username}Group
  SmtpUser:
    Type: AWS::IAM::User
    Properties:
      UserName: !Ref Username
      Groups:
        - !Ref SmtpUserGroup
  SmtpUserPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub ${Username}Policy
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - ses:SendEmail
              - ses:SendRawEmail
            Resource: '*'
      Groups:
        - !Ref SmtpUserGroup
  SmtpUserAccessKey:
    Type: AWS::IAM::AccessKey
    Properties:
      Serial: !Ref IamAccessKeyVersion
      Status: Active
      UserName: !Ref SmtpUser

  SmtpPassword:
    Type: Custom::SmtpPassword
    DependsOn: SmtpLambdaLogGroup
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !GetAtt SMTPCredentialsLambdaFunction.Arn
      Key: !GetAtt SmtpUserAccessKey.SecretAccessKey
      ParameterType: password
      UserName: !Ref Username

  SmtpUsername:
    Type: Custom::SmtpUsername
    DependsOn: SmtpLambdaLogGroup
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !GetAtt SMTPCredentialsLambdaFunction.Arn
      Key: !Ref SmtpUserAccessKey
      ParameterType: username
      UserName: !Ref Username

  SMTPLambdaExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Role assumed by Lambda to generate SMTP credentials
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: InlineSMTPLambdaExecutionRolePolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:

                  - UseCustomKMSKey

                      - kms:Decrypt
                      - kms:DescribeKey
                      - kms:CreateGrant
                      - kms:Encrypt
                    Resource:
                      - !Ref KmsKeyArn
                  - !Ref AWS::NoValue
                - Effect: Allow
                  Action:
                    - ssm:PutParameter
                    - ssm:DeleteParameter
                  Resource:
                    - !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/*-smtp-username"
                    - !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/*-smtp-password"

  SmtpLambdaLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub /aws/lambda/${SMTPCredentialsLambdaFunction}
      RetentionInDays: !Ref LambdaLogRetentionTime

# The following function is based on data from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/smtp-credentials.html
  SMTPCredentialsLambdaFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Description: Generates SMTP credentials and stores in Parameter Store
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      MemorySize: 128
      Environment:
        Variables:
          KMS_KEY_ARN: !Ref KmsKeyArn
      Role: !GetAtt SMTPLambdaExecutionRole.Arn
      Runtime: python3.13
      Timeout: 30
      Code:
        ZipFile: !Sub |
          import hmac
          import hashlib
          import base64
          import boto3
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError
          import cfnresponse
          import logging
          import os
          import logging
          from sys import exit

          # Configure logging
          logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)
          log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

          # Constants
          REGION = os.environ['AWS_REGION']
          SMTP_REGIONS = [
              "us-east-2",  # US East (Ohio)
              "us-east-1",  # US East (N. Virginia)
              "us-west-2",  # US West (Oregon)
              "ap-south-1",  # Asia Pacific (Mumbai)
              "ap-northeast-2",  # Asia Pacific (Seoul)
              "ap-southeast-1",  # Asia Pacific (Singapore)
              "ap-southeast-2",  # Asia Pacific (Sydney)
              "ap-northeast-1",  # Asia Pacific (Tokyo)
              "ca-central-1",  # Canada (Central)
              "eu-central-1",  # Europe (Frankfurt)
              "eu-west-1",  # Europe (Ireland)
              "eu-west-2",  # Europe (London)
              "eu-south-1",  # Europe (Milan)
              "eu-north-1",  # Europe (Stockholm)
              "sa-east-1",  # South America (Sao Paulo)
              "us-gov-west-1",  # AWS GovCloud (US)
              "us-gov-east-1",  # AWS GovCloud (US)
          ]
          CUSTOM_KMS_KEY = not os.environ['KMS_KEY_ARN'] == ""

          # Boto3 Clients
          ssm = boto3.client('ssm', region_name=REGION)

          # Boto3 Decorators
          """
          These Python decorators signal the success or failure of Lambda-backed CloudFormation
          custom resources. To use these resources:

          1. Since the signal requires data that will be provided by the inputs to the lambda
          handler (i.e., 'event' and 'context'), the long form of a decorator needs to be used.
          For example, if you have the following function defined in your code:

          def sample_function(params):
              ....

          Call the decorator by stating something like:
          'outcome = assess_cfn_status(event, context, data, id, False)(sample_function)(params)'

          3. The last parameter (final_step) of the assess_cfn_status function/decorator indicates
          if this is the final step of the custom resource logic. If set to "True", the decorator will
          send a success signal to CloudFormation if the result is successful. Please note that the
          function will exit without returning the result, so set it to "False" and call
          cfnresponse.send outside of the function if you need to use the result before signaling (i.e.,
          adding the output to the resource output attributes)
          """
          def send_cfn_signal(event, context, data, id, final_step=False):
              def inner(func):
                  def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
                      error = None
                      outcome = func(*args, **kwargs)
                      err_msg = "Custom resource execution failed. See the further details in CloudWatch Log Stream: {}.".format(context.log_stream_name)
                      if isinstance(outcome, dict):
                          if "CFN_Response_Status" in outcome:
                              if "Error_Message" in outcome:
                                  err_msg = outcome["Error_Message"]
                              elif "Error" in outcome:
                                  error = outcome["Error"]
                                  log.error(err_msg)
                              cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.FAILED, data, id, reason=err_msg)
                              if error is not None:
                                  raise error
                              else:
                                  exit()
                          else:
                              return outcome
                      if final_step:
                          cfnresponse.send(event, context, cfnresponse.SUCCESS, data, id)
                          exit()
                      else:
                          return outcome
                  return wrapper
              return inner

          def boto3_err_msg(func):
              def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
                  try:
                      response = func(*args, **kwargs)
                      return response
                  except ClientError as err:
                      message = err.response['Error']['Message']
                      log.error(message)
                      payload = {
                          "CFN_Response_Status": cfnresponse.FAILED,
                          "Error_Message": message
                      }
                      return payload
                  except Exception as err:
                      payload = {
                          "CFN_Response_Status": cfnresponse.FAILED,
                          "Error": err
                      }
                      log.error("Encountered error that was not a boto3 ClientError.")
                      return payload
              return wrapper

          def assess_cfn_status(event, context, data, id, final_step=False):
              def inner(boto_func):
                  def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
                      new_func = send_cfn_signal(event, context, data, id, final_step)(boto3_err_msg(boto_func))
                      result = new_func(*args, **kwargs)
                      return result
                  return wrapper
              return inner

          # These values are required to calculate the signature. Do not change them.
          DATE = "11111111"
          SERVICE = "ses"
          MESSAGE = "SendRawEmail"
          TERMINAL = "aws4_request"
          VERSION = 0x04

          def sign(key, msg):
              return hmac.new(key, msg.encode('utf-8'), hashlib.sha256).digest()

          def calculate_key(secret_access_key, region):
              if region not in SMTP_REGIONS:
                  raise ValueError(f"The {region} Region doesn't have an SMTP endpoint.")

              signature = sign(("AWS4" + secret_access_key).encode('utf-8'), DATE)
              signature = sign(signature, region)
              signature = sign(signature, SERVICE)
              signature = sign(signature, TERMINAL)
              signature = sign(signature, MESSAGE)
              signature_and_version = bytes([VERSION]) + signature
              smtp_password = base64.b64encode(signature_and_version)
              return smtp_password.decode('utf-8')

          def put_parameter(username, value, type):
                  if CUSTOM_KMS_KEY:
                      ssm.put_parameter(
                              Name=f"{username}-smtp-{type}",
                              Description=f"SMTP {type} for email communications",
                              Value=value,
                              Type='SecureString',
                              KeyId=os.environ['KMS_KEY_ARN'],
                              Overwrite=True,
                              Tier='Standard'
                          )
                  else:
                      ssm.put_parameter(
                              Name=f"{username}-smtp-{type}",
                              Description=f"SMTP {type} for email communications",
                              Value=value,
                              Type='SecureString',
                              Overwrite=True,
                              Tier='Standard'
                          )
                  return None

          def delete_smtp_credentials(username, type):
              ssm.delete_parameter(Name=f"{username}-smtp-{type}")
              return None

          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              parameter_type = event['ResourceProperties']['ParameterType']
              username = event['ResourceProperties']['UserName']
              key = event['ResourceProperties']['Key']
              parameter_arn = "arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/" + f"{username}-smtp-{parameter_type}"
              cfn_data ={}

              if event['RequestType'] == 'Create':
                  if parameter_type == 'username':
                      assess_cfn_status(event, context, cfn_data, parameter_arn, True)(put_parameter)(username, key, parameter_type)
                  elif parameter_type == 'password':
                      pwd = assess_cfn_status(event, context, cfn_data, parameter_arn, False)(calculate_key)(key, REGION)
                      assess_cfn_status(event, context, cfn_data, parameter_arn, True)(put_parameter)(username, pwd, parameter_type)
              elif event['RequestType'] == 'Update':
                  name_change = False
                  if "OldResourceProperties" in event:
                      old_username = event['OldResourceProperties']['UserName']
                      if username != old_username:
                          name_change = True
                  final = not name_change
                  if parameter_type == 'username':
                      assess_cfn_status(event, context, cfn_data, parameter_arn, final)(put_parameter)(username, key, parameter_type)
                  elif parameter_type == 'password':
                      pwd = assess_cfn_status(event, context, cfn_data, parameter_arn, False)(calculate_key)(key, REGION)
                      assess_cfn_status(event, context, cfn_data, parameter_arn, final)(put_parameter)(username, pwd, parameter_type)
                  if name_change:
                      assess_cfn_status(event, context, cfn_data, parameter_arn, name_change)(delete_smtp_credentials)(old_username, parameter_type)
              elif event['RequestType'] == 'Delete':
                  assess_cfn_status(event, context, cfn_data, parameter_arn, True)(delete_smtp_credentials)(username, parameter_type)

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates the IAM roles and instance profile needed to support a CodeDeploy and CodePipeline based release pipeline demo. It should include an EC2 instance role and matching instance profile granting broad administrative access for testing purposes, a CodeDeploy service role that can be assumed by the CodeDeploy service in the us-east-1 and us-west-2 regions with permissions to describe EC2 instances and manage Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks for blue/green style deployments, and a CodePipeline service role with the permissions needed to read and write pipeline artifacts in S3 and to orchestrate deployments across Elastic Beanstalk, EC2, Elastic Load Balancing, Auto Scaling, CloudWatch, S3, CloudFormation, RDS, SQS, ECS, CodeDeploy, and Lambda, including the ability to pass IAM roles to those services.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a serverless webhook handler wiring together Stripe payments and our Squarespace Commerce store to post sales notifications to Slack. It should provision an API Gateway REST API with a POST /webhooks endpoint, deployed to a prod stage, backed by a Lambda function that parses an incoming Stripe webhook event, looks up the corresponding Squarespace order and its inventory details, and publishes a formatted notification message to an SNS topic that the stack also creates for relaying to Slack. The template should include the Lambda function's execution role (with permission to publish to that topic), the permission allowing API Gateway to invoke the function, a CloudWatch alarm that triggers whenever the function's invocation errors exceed zero within a one-minute period, and the function's log group. The Squarespace API token and the Stripe webhook signing secret should be accepted as required input parameters so no secrets are hardcoded in the template.

We need a CloudFormation template that creates a self-contained test environment for an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis replication group with cluster mode enabled, spread across two Availability Zones for resilience testing purposes. It should build its own VPC (defaulting to a 10.0.0.0/22 CIDR block) with two private subnets in different Availability Zones (defaulting to 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24), a security group permitting traffic between those subnets, and an ElastiCache subnet group. The replication group should have Multi-AZ and automatic failover enabled, two shards with one replica each, and both at-rest and in-transit encryption turned on using a customer-managed KMS key that the stack also creates. It should also include an SNS topic, encrypted with that same key, with a policy allowing CloudWatch to publish alarm notifications to it, and an IAM role with a minimal policy allowing it to send SSM Automation signals, to support an automated approval step in a resilience or gameday testing runbook.

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31
Description: Lab 4.5 — Cognito User Pool + JWT-protected REST API

Resources:

  UserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: dva-lab-04-05-pool
      AutoVerifiedAttributes: [email]
      UsernameAttributes: [email]
      Policies:
        PasswordPolicy:
          MinimumLength: 8
          RequireUppercase: true
          RequireLowercase: true
          RequireNumbers: true
          RequireSymbols: true
      Schema:
        - Name: email
          AttributeDataType: String
          Required: true
          Mutable: true

  UserPoolClient:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    Properties:
      ClientName: dva-lab-04-05-cli
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      GenerateSecret: false
      ExplicitAuthFlows:
        - ALLOW_ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH
        - ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH
        - ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH
      AccessTokenValidity: 60       # 60 minutes
      IdTokenValidity: 60
      RefreshTokenValidity: 30      # 30 days
      TokenValidityUnits:
        AccessToken: minutes
        IdToken: minutes
        RefreshToken: days

  RestApi:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi
    Properties:
      Name: dva-lab-04-05-api
      EndpointConfiguration:
        Types: [REGIONAL]

  Authorizer:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Authorizer
    Properties:
      Name: dva-lab-04-05-cognito-authorizer
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      Type: COGNITO_USER_POOLS
      IdentitySource: method.request.header.Authorization
      ProviderARNs:
        - !GetAtt UserPool.Arn

  EchoFunction:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: dva-lab-04-05-echo
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      InlineCode: |
        import json
        def handler(event, context):
            ctx = event.get("requestContext", {})
            authorizer = ctx.get("authorizer", {})
            claims = authorizer.get("claims", {})
            return {
                "statusCode": 200,
                "headers": {"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                "body": json.dumps({
                    "path": event.get("path"),
                    "method": event.get("httpMethod"),
                    "claims": claims,
                    "message": (
                        "you are authenticated as " + claims.get("email", "unknown")
                        if claims else "open endpoint — no claims"
                    ),
                }),
            }

  ## /me — protected
  MeResource:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Resource
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      ParentId: !GetAtt RestApi.RootResourceId
      PathPart: me

  MeMethod:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Method
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      ResourceId: !Ref MeResource
      HttpMethod: GET
      AuthorizationType: COGNITO_USER_POOLS
      AuthorizerId: !Ref Authorizer
      Integration:
        Type: AWS_PROXY
        IntegrationHttpMethod: POST
        Uri: !Sub arn:aws:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${EchoFunction.Arn}/invocations

  ## /open — unauthenticated comparison
  OpenResource:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Resource
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      ParentId: !GetAtt RestApi.RootResourceId
      PathPart: open

  OpenMethod:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Method
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      ResourceId: !Ref OpenResource
      HttpMethod: GET
      AuthorizationType: NONE
      Integration:
        Type: AWS_PROXY
        IntegrationHttpMethod: POST
        Uri: !Sub arn:aws:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${EchoFunction.Arn}/invocations

  EchoFunctionPermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !Ref EchoFunction
      Principal: apigateway.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !Sub arn:aws:execute-api:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RestApi}/*/*/*

  Deployment:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Deployment
    DependsOn: [MeMethod, OpenMethod]
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      Description: Lab 4.5 deployment

  Stage:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Stage
    Properties:
      StageName: prod
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      DeploymentId: !Ref Deployment

Outputs:
  UserPoolId:
    Value: !Ref UserPool
    Export:
      Name: dva-lab-04-05-user-pool-id
  UserPoolArn:
    Value: !GetAtt UserPool.Arn
    Export:
      Name: dva-lab-04-05-user-pool-arn
  ClientId:
    Value: !Ref UserPoolClient
    Export:
      Name: dva-lab-04-05-client-id
  ApiUrl:
    Value: !Sub https://${RestApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/prod

prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that connects our AWS account to the third-party marbot.io monitoring and alerting service. Given our marbot endpoint ID as a parameter, it should set up an EventBridge API destination and connection, authenticated with an API key derived from that endpoint ID, along with a scheduled rule that runs every 30 days to post our account and stack identification details to marbot's service in order to establish and keep the connection alive, plus the IAM role EventBridge needs to invoke that destination. The template should also create a cross-account IAM role that marbot's AWS account can assume, using an external ID unique to this stack, to perform monitoring on our behalf, with permissions gated behind separate boolean feature flags for automatically configuring CloudWatch alarms and monitoring rules across our resources, enriching account IDs with friendly aliases, embedding metric graphs into CloudWatch alarm notifications, and approving or rejecting CodePipeline manual approval requests. When the automatic monitoring feature is enabled, that role's own permissions to manage its resources should additionally be restricted by an IAM permissions boundary policy created by the stack. Finally, the template should register the account connection with marbot's service using a custom resource.

Metadata:

    ParameterGroups:
    - Label:
        default: 'marbot endpoint'
      Parameters:
      - EndpointId
      - Stage
    - Label:
        default: 'Features'
      Parameters:
      - MonitoringAssistant
      - AccountAlias
      - CloudWatchMetricGraph
      - CodePipelineApproval
Parameters:
  EndpointId:
    Description: 'Your marbot endpoint ID (to get this value: select a channel where marbot belongs to and send a message like this: "@marbot show me my endpoint id").'
    Type: String
  Stage:
    Description: 'marbot stage (never change this!).'
    Type: String
    Default: v1
    AllowedValues: [v1, dev]
  MonitoringAssistant:
    Description: 'Configure AWS monitoring rules automatically?'
    Type: String
    Default: true
    AllowedValues: [true, false]
  AccountAlias:
    Description: 'Enrich AWS account IDs with alias names?'
    Type: String
    Default: true
    AllowedValues: [true, false]
  CloudWatchMetricGraph:
    Description: 'Enrich CloudWatch Alarms with metric graphs?'
    Type: String
    Default: true
    AllowedValues: [true, false]
  CodePipelineApproval:
    Description: 'Allow CodePipeline approval requests to be approved or rejected with a button?'
    Type: String
    Default: true
    AllowedValues: [true, false]
Conditions:
  MonitoringAssistantEnabled: !Equals [!Ref MonitoringAssistant, 'true']
  AccountAliasEnabled: !Equals [!Ref AccountAlias, 'true']
  CloudWatchMetricGraphEnabled: !Equals [!Ref CloudWatchMetricGraph, 'true']
  CodePipelineApprovalEnabled: !Equals [!Ref CodePipelineApproval, 'true']
Resources:
  ##########################################################################
  #                                                                        #
  #                                  API                                   #
  #                                                                        #
  ##########################################################################
  ApiConnection:
    Type: 'AWS::Events::Connection'
    Properties:
      AuthorizationType: 'API_KEY'
      AuthParameters:
        ApiKeyAuthParameters:
          ApiKeyName: 'X-API-Key'
          ApiKeyValue: !Ref EndpointId
      Description: 'marbot'
  ApiDestination:
    Type: 'AWS::Events::ApiDestination'
    Properties:
      ConnectionArn: !GetAtt 'ApiConnection.Arn'
      Description: 'Forwards notifiations and alarms to marbot'
      HttpMethod: 'POST'
      InvocationEndpoint: !Sub 'https://api.marbot.io/${Stage}/endpoint/${EndpointId}'
      InvocationRateLimitPerSecond: 1
  ApiRole:
    Type: 'AWS::IAM::Role'
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
        - Effect: 'Allow'
          Principal:
            Service:
            - 'events.amazonaws.com'
          Action:
          - sts:AssumeRole
      Path: '/service-role/'
      Policies:
      - PolicyName: eventbridge
        PolicyDocument:
          Version: '2012-10-17'
          Statement:
          - Effect: 'Allow'
            Action: 'events:InvokeApiDestination'
            Resource: !GetAtt 'ApiDestination.Arn'
  MonitoringJumpStartEvent:
    Type: 'AWS::Events::Rule'
    Properties:
      Description: 'Monitoring Jump Start connection. (created by marbot)'
      ScheduleExpression: 'rate(30 days)'
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
      - Arn: !GetAtt 'ApiDestination.Arn'
        Id: marbot
        RoleArn: !GetAtt 'ApiRole.Arn'
        Input: !Sub |
          {
            "Type": "monitoring-jump-start-connection",
            "StackTemplate": "marbot-aws-account-connection",
            "StackVersion": "1.3.1",
            "Partition": "${AWS::Partition}",
            "AccountId": "${AWS::AccountId}",
            "Region": "${AWS::Region}",
            "StackId": "${AWS::StackId}",
            "StackName": "${AWS::StackName}"

  ##########################################################################
  #                                                                        #
  #                         AWS ACCOUNT CONNECTION                         #
  #                                                                        #
  ##########################################################################
  PermissionsBoundaryPolicy:
    Condition: MonitoringAssistantEnabled
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Type: 'AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy'
    Properties:
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
          - 'cloudwatch:describeAlarms'
          - 'securityhub:BatchUpdateFindings'
          Resource: '*'
        - Effect: Allow
          Action: 'sns:Publish'
          Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:sns:*:${AWS::AccountId}:marbot*'
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
          - 'logs:CreateLogStream'
          - 'logs:PutLogEvents'
          Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:*:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/marbot*'
  Role:
    Type: 'AWS::IAM::Role'
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
        - Effect: Allow
          Principal:
            AWS: '853553028582'
          Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
          Condition:
            StringEquals:
              'sts:ExternalId': !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]
      Policies:
      - !If
        - MonitoringAssistantEnabled
        - PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
            - Effect: Allow
              Action:
              - 'elasticloadbalancing:DescribeLoadBalancers'
              - 'elasticloadbalancing:DescribeTargetGroups'
              - 'elasticloadbalancing:DescribeTags'
              - 'elasticloadbalancing:DescribeLoadBalancerAttributes'
              - 'elasticloadbalancing:DescribeTargetGroupAttributes'
              - 'autoscaling:DescribeAutoScalingGroups'
              - 'ec2:DescribeInstances'
              - 'rds:DescribeDBClusters'
              - 'rds:ListTagsForResource'
              - 'sqs:ListQueues'
              - 'sqs:GetQueueUrl'
              - 'sqs:ListQueueTags'
              - 'sqs:GetQueueAttributes'
              - 'ec2:DescribeAccountAttributes'
              - 'ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute'
              - 'ec2:DescribeInstanceCreditSpecifications'
              - 'ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes'
              - 'ec2:DescribeVolumes'
              - 'ec2:DescribeVpcs'
              - 'sts:GetCallerIdentity'
              - 'logs:DescribeLogGroups'
              - 'sns:GetSubscriptionAttributes' # no resource-level restrictions supported
              - 'sns:SetSubscriptionAttributes' # no resource-level restrictions supported
              - 'sns:Unsubscribe' # no resource-level restrictions supported
              Resource: '*'
            - Effect: Allow
              Action:
              - 'budgets:ModifyBudget'
              - 'budgets:ViewBudget'
              Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:budgets::${AWS::AccountId}:budget/marbot*'
            - Effect: Allow
              Action:
              - 'cloudwatch:DeleteAlarms'
              - 'cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms'
              - 'cloudwatch:ListTagsForResource'
              - 'cloudwatch:PutMetricAlarm'
              - 'cloudwatch:TagResource'
              - 'cloudwatch:UntagResource'
              Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudwatch:*:${AWS::AccountId}:alarm:marbot*'
            - Effect: Allow
              Action:
              - 'events:DeleteRule'
              - 'events:DescribeRule'
              - 'events:ListTagsForResource'
              - 'events:ListTargetsByRule'
              - 'events:PutRule'
              - 'events:PutTargets'
              - 'events:RemoveTargets'
              - 'events:TagResource'
              - 'events:UntagResource'
              Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:*:${AWS::AccountId}:rule/marbot*'
            - Effect: Allow
              Action:
              - 'sns:CreateTopic'
              - 'sns:DeleteTopic'
              - 'sns:GetTopicAttributes'
              - 'sns:ListTagsForResource'
              - 'sns:SetTopicAttributes'
              - 'sns:Subscribe'
              - 'sns:TagResource'
              - 'sns:UntagResource'
              Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:sns:*:${AWS::AccountId}:marbot*'
            - Effect: Allow
              Action:
              - 'rds:CreateEventSubscription'
              - 'rds:DeleteEventSubscription'
              - 'rds:AddSourceIdentifierToSubscription'
              - 'rds:RemoveSourceIdentifierFromSubscription'
              - 'rds:DescribeEventSubscriptions'
              - 'rds:ListTagsForResource'
              - 'rds:ModifyEventSubscription'
              - 'rds:AddTagsToResource'
              - 'rds:RemoveTagsFromResource'
              Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:rds:*:${AWS::AccountId}:es:marbot*'
            - Effect: Allow
              Action:
              - 'logs:CreateLogGroup'
              - 'logs:DeleteLogGroup'
              - 'logs:DeleteRetentionPolicy'
              - 'logs:ListTagsLogGroup'
              - 'logs:PutRetentionPolicy'
              - 'logs:TagLogGroup'
              - 'logs:TagResource'
              - 'logs:UntagLogGroup'
              - 'logs:UntagResource'
              Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:*:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/marbot*'
            - Effect: Allow

              - 'lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration'
              - 'lambda:UpdateFunctionCode'
              - 'lambda:DeleteFunction'
              - 'lambda:GetFunction'
              - 'lambda:GetFunctionCodeSigningConfig'
              - 'lambda:GetPolicy'
              - 'lambda:ListVersionsByFunction'
              - 'lambda:RemovePermission'
              - 'lambda:ListTags'
              - 'lambda:TagResource'

              - 'iam:PutRolePolicy'
              - 'iam:PutRolePermissionsBoundary'

              Condition:

            - Effect: Allow

            - Effect: Allow

              - 'iam:DeleteRole'
              - 'iam:GetRole'
              - 'iam:GetRolePolicy'
              - 'iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies'
              - 'iam:ListInstanceProfilesForRole'
              - 'iam:ListRolePolicies'
              - 'iam:UpdateRoleDescription'
              - 'iam:ListRoleTags'
              - 'iam:TagRole'
              - 'iam:UntagRole'

        - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'

It should provision a DynamoDB table with a numeric id as the partition key, provisioned for 10 read and 10 write capacity units, plus a global secondary index also keyed on id with 5 read and 10 write capacity units. It should also create a Cognito identity pool that allows unauthenticated guest access, along with the IAM role assumed by unauthenticated identities and the identity pool role attachment linking the two. prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Glue Data Catalog database along with an optional crawler and an optional Spark ETL job, forming the catalog and transform layer of a data lake. It should accept a naming prefix and an environment (dev, staging, or prod) used to build the database, crawler, and job names, along with the ARN and prefix of an existing S3 bucket that the crawler scans for schema and partition discovery. The crawler should run on a configurable cron schedule (defaulting to once daily), only log rather than automatically apply schema and partition changes it detects, only scan newly added data on each run, and be toggleable on or off through a parameter (off changes nothing about the catalog itself). The ETL job, also toggleable and off by default, should be a Glue Spark job with a configurable worker type, worker count, timeout, and maximum concurrent runs, reading its script from an S3 location supplied as a parameter, writing transformed output under a separate target S3 bucket and prefix, using job bookmarks so reruns only process new data, and logging continuously to a CloudWatch log group with a configurable retention period. Both the crawler and the job should share one IAM service role scoped to read access on the source bucket and, when a target bucket is supplied, write access on that target bucket as well.

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"

Description: >-
  Glue Data Catalog database, a crawler over an S3 prefix, and a scheduled Spark
  ETL job with bookmarks - the catalog and transform half of a data lake.

Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: Naming
        Parameters:
          - NamePrefix
          - Environment
          - DatabaseSuffix
      - Label:
          default: Source data
        Parameters:
          - SourceBucketArn
          - SourcePrefix
      - Label:
          default: Output
        Parameters:
          - TargetBucketArn
          - TargetPrefix
      - Label:
          default: Crawler
        Parameters:
          - CrawlerSchedule
          - EnableCrawler
      - Label:
          default: ETL job
        Parameters:
          - EnableJob
          - JobScriptS3Uri
          - GlueVersion
          - WorkerType
          - NumberOfWorkers
          - JobTimeoutMinutes
          - MaxConcurrentRuns
      - Label:
          default: Operations
        Parameters:
          - LogRetentionDays

Parameters:
  NamePrefix:
    Type: String
    Description: Prefix for the database, crawler and job names.
    AllowedPattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,30}[a-z0-9]$"
    ConstraintDescription: 3-32 lowercase characters, digits and hyphens.

  Environment:
    Type: String
    Description: Environment this catalog serves.
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues: [dev, staging, prod]

  DatabaseSuffix:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Catalog database name suffix, e.g. "raw" or "curated". Glue database names
      use underscores, so hyphens in NamePrefix are converted.
    Default: raw
    AllowedPattern: "^[a-z0-9_]{1,60}$"

  SourceBucketArn:
    Type: String
    Description: ARN of the bucket the crawler reads and the job takes input from.

  SourcePrefix:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Prefix the crawler scans, e.g. "raw/clickstream". Point it at the table
      root, above the partition directories - a crawler pointed inside the
      partitions registers each one as a separate table.
    Default: raw

  TargetBucketArn:
    Type: String
    Description: ARN of the bucket the ETL job writes to. May be the same bucket.
    Default: ""

  TargetPrefix:
    Type: String
    Description: Prefix the job writes transformed data under.
    Default: curated

  EnableCrawler:
    Type: String
    Description: Create the crawler that discovers schema and partitions.
    Default: "true"
    AllowedValues: ["true", "false"]

  CrawlerSchedule:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Cron expression for the crawler, in UTC, e.g. "cron(0 1 * * ? *)" for
      01:00 daily. Leave empty to run it on demand only.
    Default: "cron(0 1 * * ? *)"

  EnableJob:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Create the Spark ETL job. Off by default - a catalog and a crawler are
      useful on their own, and a job with no script is just a failing resource.
    Default: "false"
    AllowedValues: ["true", "false"]

  JobScriptS3Uri:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      s3:// URI of the PySpark or Scala script. Version the key: Glue reads the
      script at run time, so overwriting it changes what runs without any
      CloudFormation event to show for it.
    Default: ""

  GlueVersion:
    Type: String
    Description: Glue runtime version, which fixes the Spark and Python versions.
    Default: "4.0"
    AllowedValues: ["3.0", "4.0", "5.0"]

  WorkerType:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      G.1X is 4 vCPU / 16 GB per worker and the sensible starting point. G.2X
      doubles both, for wide joins or skewed data. G.025X is a quarter worker for
      small streaming jobs.
    Default: G.1X
    AllowedValues: [G.1X, G.2X, G.4X, G.8X, G.025X]

  NumberOfWorkers:
    Type: Number
    Description: >-
      Workers per run. Glue bills per DPU-hour with a 1-minute minimum, so
      over-provisioning a short job is a direct multiplier on cost.
    Default: 2
    MinValue: 2
    MaxValue: 299

  JobTimeoutMinutes:
    Type: Number
    Description: >-
      Kill the run after this long. Glue's own default is 2880 minutes - two
      days - which on a hung job is an expensive way to find out.
    Default: 60
    MinValue: 1
    MaxValue: 2880

  MaxConcurrentRuns:
    Type: Number
    Description: >-
      Simultaneous runs allowed. Keep it at 1 unless the job is genuinely
      partitioned by input: two concurrent runs with bookmarks enabled will
      process overlapping data.
    Default: 1
    MinValue: 1
    MaxValue: 100

  LogRetentionDays:
    Type: Number
    Description: Retention for the job's log group.
    Default: 30
    AllowedValues: [1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 365, 400, 545, 731, 1827, 3653]

Conditions:
  ShouldCreateCrawler: !Equals [!Ref EnableCrawler, "true"]
  HasCrawlerSchedule: !And
    - !Condition ShouldCreateCrawler
    - !Not [!Equals [!Ref CrawlerSchedule, ""]]
  ShouldCreateJob: !Equals [!Ref EnableJob, "true"]
  HasTargetBucket: !Not [!Equals [!Ref TargetBucketArn, ""]]

Resources:
  Database:
    Type: AWS::Glue::Database
    Properties:
      CatalogId: !Ref AWS::AccountId
      DatabaseInput:
        # Glue database names reject hyphens, so the prefix is joined with
        # underscores rather than passed through.
        Name: !Sub
          - "${Prefix}_${Environment}_${DatabaseSuffix}"
          - Prefix: !Join ["_", !Split ["-", !Ref NamePrefix]]
        Description: !Sub "${NamePrefix} ${DatabaseSuffix} catalog (${Environment})"

  ServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: glue.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref AWS::AccountId
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        # Grants catalog access and CloudWatch logging. It does *not* grant S3
        # access to your buckets — that is the inline policy below, scoped to
        # exactly the two buckets this stack was given.
        - !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSGlueServiceRole"
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: lake-access
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:ListBucket
                Resource:
                  - !Ref SourceBucketArn
                  - !Sub "${SourceBucketArn}/*"
              - !If
                - HasTargetBucket
                - Effect: Allow
                  Action:
                    - s3:PutObject
                    - s3:DeleteObject
                    - s3:ListBucket
                  Resource:
                    - !Ref TargetBucketArn
                    - !Sub "${TargetBucketArn}/*"
                - !Ref AWS::NoValue

  Crawler:
    Type: AWS::Glue::Crawler
    Condition: ShouldCreateCrawler
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${NamePrefix}-${Environment}-${DatabaseSuffix}"
      Role: !GetAtt ServiceRole.Arn
      DatabaseName: !Ref Database
      Targets:
        S3Targets:
          - Path: !Sub
              - "s3://${BucketName}/${SourcePrefix}/"
              - BucketName: !Select [5, !Split [":", !Ref SourceBucketArn]]
      Schedule: !If
        - HasCrawlerSchedule
        - ScheduleExpression: !Ref CrawlerSchedule
        - !Ref AWS::NoValue
      SchemaChangePolicy:
        # LOG rather than UPDATE_IN_DATABASE: an automatic schema update on a
        # column type change silently rewrites the table definition, and every
        # query that relied on the old type starts failing or, worse, coercing.
        UpdateBehavior: LOG
        # A deleted partition is far more often a lifecycle rule doing its job
        # than a table that should vanish.
        DeleteBehavior: LOG
      RecrawlPolicy:
        # Only scan what arrived since the last run. A full recrawl of a large
        # lake is slow and bills for every object listed.
        RecrawlBehavior: CRAWL_NEW_FOLDERS_ONLY
      Configuration: |
        {"Version":1.0,"CrawlerOutput":{"Partitions":{"AddOrUpdateBehavior":"InheritFromTable"}}}

  JobLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Condition: ShouldCreateJob
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub "/${Environment}/${NamePrefix}/glue/${DatabaseSuffix}"
      RetentionInDays: !Ref LogRetentionDays

  Job:
    Type: AWS::Glue::Job
    Condition: ShouldCreateJob
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${NamePrefix}-${Environment}-${DatabaseSuffix}-etl"
      Role: !GetAtt ServiceRole.Arn
      GlueVersion: !Ref GlueVersion
      WorkerType: !Ref WorkerType
      NumberOfWorkers: !Ref NumberOfWorkers
      Timeout: !Ref JobTimeoutMinutes
      ExecutionProperty:
        MaxConcurrentRuns: !Ref MaxConcurrentRuns
      Command:
        Name: glueetl
        PythonVersion: "3"
        ScriptLocation: !Ref JobScriptS3Uri
      DefaultArguments:
        # Bookmarks make a rerun process only new data. Without them, a job
        # scheduled hourly reprocesses the entire lake every hour.
        "--job-bookmark-option": job-bookmark-enable
        "--enable-metrics": "true"
        "--enable-continuous-cloudwatch-log": "true"
        "--continuous-log-logGroup": !Ref JobLogGroup
        "--enable-spark-ui": "false"
        "--TempDir": !Sub
          - "s3://${BucketName}/${TargetPrefix}/_glue_temp/"
          - BucketName: !Select
              - 5
              - !Split [":", !If [HasTargetBucket, !Ref TargetBucketArn, !Ref SourceBucketArn]]

Outputs:
  DatabaseName:
    Description: Glue Data Catalog database name, for Athena queries and job scripts.
    Value: !Ref Database

  ServiceRoleArn:
    Description: Role the crawler and job assume.
    Value: !GetAtt ServiceRole.Arn

  CrawlerName:
    Description: Crawler name, for on-demand runs via start-crawler.
    Condition: ShouldCreateCrawler
    Value: !Ref Crawler

  JobName:
    Description: ETL job name, for start-job-run and for Step Functions.
    Condition: ShouldCreateJob
    Value: !Ref Job
